Investors may care because disintermediating legacy supermarket chains captures better margins while capitalizing on structural demand for transparent, resilient food supply chains.

q-hyrdon.summary: Hyrdon provides all-inclusive car subscriptions covering maintenance, insurance, and taxes to Swedish consumers and businesses. The company operates across three regional hubs, managing roughly 700 active subscriptions with access to around 1,500 vehicles, while external funding remains undisclosed. Investors may value its recurring-revenue model, which capitalizes on the accelerating shift from traditional car ownership to flexible mobility.

q-napper.summary: Napper sells an AI-driven baby sleep tracking and routine-optimizing subscription app directly to parents. Backed by Accel and VNV Global, the startup grew revenue to nearly SEK 61 million in 2024 while remaining profitable. Investors will appreciate its capital-efficient growth, strong Nordic market penetration, and proven ability to monetize a universal parenting pain point.

q-curb.summary: Curb operated dark kitchens creating data-driven, delivery-only food brands sold to consumers via apps like Foodora and Wolt. Founded by former Delivery Hero executives, it raised over €23 million from EQT Ventures and Point72 Ventures before shutting down in 2022. Investors were drawn to the founders' proven industry pedigree and data-led approach, though its fate highlights the severe capital intensity of ghost kitchens.

c03ec927-2d92-49b0-b766-c82f90625906.summary: Banky operates a consumer credit platform offering unsecured and guarantor-backed loans to Swedish consumers who have weaker credit profiles or are underserved by traditional banks. Partnering with lender Bankaktiebolaget Nordiska, it acts as a credit intermediary and generated approximately 20 million SEK in 2023 revenue. Investors may appreciate its asset-light model that captures high-margin non-prime demand while mitigating default risk through guarantors.

q-demaai.summary: Dema.ai sells a predictive analytics platform to e-commerce brands, delivering real-time insights on marketing spend, inventory, and customer lifetime value. The Stockholm-based startup has raised €11 million, including a €7 million seed round in 2024 led by J12 Ventures and Daphni. An investor might care because it addresses a critical market shift away from vanity revenue toward sustainable, unit-level profitability.

q-womni.summary: Womni operates a digital clinic providing specialized consultations, testing, and treatment plans for women navigating menopause and hormonal health issues. Bootstrapped without venture capital beyond an early Vinnova grant, the business has doubled its revenue while achieving profitability. Investors may value its ability to generate sustainable margins in digital health by establishing a viable, out-of-pocket private-pay model outside public reimbursement systems.

q-klimio.summary: Klimio provides end-to-end heat pump sales and installation services to residential homeowners in Sweden. It partnered with utility Ellevio and reached over 32 million SEK in revenue before entering bankruptcy proceedings in late 2025. Investors track this segment because residential electrification offers a massive decarbonization market, while highlighting the severe working-capital and execution hurdles of scaling home installations.

q-chargehome.summary: Chargehome sells and installs EV chargers, battery storage, and energy management systems directly to Swedish homeowners, housing cooperatives, and commercial properties. After generating 15.6 million SEK in 2024 revenue, its core assets and digital platform were acquired by Windon Energy Group in late 2025. Investors should note it highlights rising residential demand for electrification alongside the severe margin pressures facing installation startups.

q-findmyfactory.summary: Find My Factory, rebranded as Speya, develops an AI-powered supplier intelligence platform that automates manufacturer discovery and qualification for corporate procurement teams in retail, food, and manufacturing. The Stockholm-based startup raised 13 million SEK at a post-money valuation near 100 million SEK. Investors may care because its autonomous search agents address surging demand for supply chain resilience and diversification by significantly cutting manual sourcing cycles.

q-nexta.summary: Based in Karlstad, Nexta provides a modular, headless SaaS e-commerce platform bundled with design and integrations for Nordic small and mid-sized consumer retailers. The 13-person team has deployed stores for clients like Färjestad BK and Lecab, though outside funding remains undisclosed. Investors may value its ability to make flexible headless architecture accessible to regional merchants without enterprise costs or vendor lock-in.

q-greenely.summary: Greenely provides a home energy management platform and dynamic electricity contracts to consumers, orchestrating assets like heat pumps, home batteries, and electric vehicles to lower power bills. The company has raised over €8 million in Series A funding and serves roughly 200,000 Swedish households while expanding across the Nordics. Investors may value its virtual power plant capabilities, which unlock revenue through grid-balancing flexibility markets.

q-hookedfoods.summary: Hooked Foods developed plant-based seafood and poultry alternatives, such as vegan tuna and salmon, sold to European supermarkets and restaurants. The startup raised over $6 million and secured listings across hundreds of stores in Sweden and Germany before filing for bankruptcy in January 2026. Investors should note it as a cautionary case study on unit economics and supply chain fragility in alternative proteins.

q-happi.summary: Stockholm-based hAppi produces prebiotic, high-fiber functional sodas sold to health-conscious consumers online and through retail partners across nine countries. The startup has secured early-stage angel and seed funding to drive its international rollout. An investor might care because the brand is positioned to capitalize on growing consumer demand for gut-health alternatives to traditional soft drinks.

4ac538f7-0e56-508f-8c72-ed938a41cea4.summary: Stockholm-based QA.tech builds an AI-powered autonomous testing platform that automates end-to-end quality assurance for software developers and web applications. The startup has raised €4 million in funding, including a €3 million seed round led by PROfounders, and serves dozens of beta customers. An investor might care because automating repetitive manual testing addresses a major developer bottleneck in the expanding software development market.

q-idealofsweden.summary: iDeal of Sweden sells fashion-forward phone cases, bags, and mobile tech accessories directly to consumers and through retail partners. The company raised nearly $10 million in funding and scaled to roughly 1 billion SEK in revenue before private equity firm Altor acquired a majority stake in 2019. Investors care because it demonstrated how to turn commodity tech accessories into high-margin, influencer-driven lifestyle brands.

q-safello.summary: Safello operates a cryptocurrency brokerage platform allowing Nordic retail consumers and businesses to buy, sell, and store digital assets via local payment rails like BankID and Swish. Listed on Nasdaq First North since 2021, the company serves over 425,000 customers and supplies crypto services to Swedish state authorities. Investors may value its licensed MiCA status and established regional footprint, offering regulatory defensibility against international competitors.

q-itbmed.summary: ITBMed develops immunomodulatory biologics, led by its monoclonal antibody siplizumab, for organ transplant recipients and patients with autoimmune conditions. The Stockholm-based biotech has raised over $67 million in funding led by Royalty Pharma's founder and has advanced into clinical trials. Investors value its potential to induce immune tolerance, which could eliminate the need for lifelong, toxic immunosuppressive drugs in transplant patients.

52613251-1227-40f1-87a3-932463cad74d.summary: Cerve provides a B2B data infrastructure and ordering platform that automates sales and ERP integrations for food distributors, wholesalers, and commercial buyers. Operating across the Nordics and the UK with over 2,000 connected businesses, the startup raised a £3.5 million seed round led by SuperSeed. Investors may value its ability to digitize a fragmented, paper-heavy supply chain where deep operational integration creates strong customer lock-in.

e26962cd-c4e0-4e9c-a749-0bfba4b0202e.summary: Gesynta Pharma develops oral, non-hormonal therapeutics targeting mPGES-1 for patients suffering from chronic inflammatory conditions, primarily endometriosis. The clinical-stage biotech has raised over SEK 340 million, including a Series B round backed by Innovestor Life Science and Industrifonden, to fund Phase II trials. Investors may value its first-in-class mechanism addressing substantial unmet needs in women's health without relying on hormonal treatments.

a33b6ffd-f928-4910-bee7-aca099a39001.summary: Elypta develops metabolism-based liquid biopsy kits and software for healthcare providers to detect early-stage cancers and monitor recurrence using blood and urine samples. The company has raised over $27 million, including a $21 million Series A led by Bonnier Ventures. Investors may care because its metabolic profiling can identify stage-one tumors that standard DNA-based liquid biopsies frequently miss.

c2a994a9-b401-449d-b385-254c52c85544.summary: Tink launched in Sweden as a consumer personal finance app before developing open banking APIs that provide financial data aggregation and payment initiation to banks and fintechs. Before being acquired by Visa for roughly 1.8 billion euros in 2022, it raised over 300 million dollars from institutional investors. Investors care because it validated that open banking infrastructure can disrupt legacy payment rails and yield major exits.

236c3254-63b5-4231-9a33-0fa99dd05bd3.summary: CELLINK develops and sells 3D bioprinters and standardized bioinks to academic and pharmaceutical researchers for tissue engineering and drug discovery. It went public on Nasdaq Stockholm, later expanding under parent company BICO Group after reaching a unicorn valuation. Investors care because its accessible hardware platform drives high-margin, recurring consumable bioink sales across the rapidly growing regenerative medicine market.

q-vippsnowvippsmobilepay.summary: Vipps MobilePay provides peer-to-peer transfers, in-store tap-to-pay, and online checkout solutions to consumers and merchants across the Nordics. The platform serves over 12 million users and 400,000 businesses, generating over NOK 2 billion in annual revenue. Investors value its dominant regional network effects and bank backing, which provide an entrenched defense against global wallets like Apple Pay.

q-neonomics.summary: Neonomics sells open finance infrastructure, offering account-to-account payment initiation and enriched financial data APIs to European businesses, fintechs, and software platforms. The company recently raised $4 million from existing shareholders and grew new customer acquisition by over 60% while halving operating costs. Investors may care because it is transitioning from pure connectivity to higher-margin financial data intelligence on a lean cost base.

q-obliquetherapeutics.summary: Oblique Therapeutics uses its proprietary AbiProt platform to discover and develop antibody drugs against previously undruggable targets in severe pain and cancer, partnering with global pharmaceutical companies. The company secured a multi-target research collaboration with Eli Lilly that includes milestone and royalty potential. Investors may care because its platform unlocks high-value, historically inaccessible drug targets, creating significant licensing upside without bearing full clinical development costs.

3141d19d-9118-459c-a5e8-8bb18154c304.summary: ZTL Payment Solution sells embedded open-banking APIs to ERP, payroll, and accounting software providers, allowing businesses to execute domestic and cross-border payments directly within their workflows. Regulated by the Financial Supervisory Authority of Norway, the company has raised around $14 million and serves tens of thousands of Nordic businesses. Investors may value its ability to disintermediate high-margin corporate banking services through seamless software integrations.

8d040a9d-2a72-4894-ab2c-9c61c3d6e766.summary: Dintero provides a unified checkout and split-payment platform for merchants and marketplaces, integrating popular Nordic payment methods alongside major credit cards. The startup has raised over $3.8 million from backers including Schibsted and Bring Ventures. Investors might care because Dintero secured direct acquirer licenses for Visa and Mastercard, enabling it to bypass intermediary banks and capture higher margins across the entire transaction chain.

q-zeipt.summary: Zeipt provides an API-based smart receipt platform that connects retailers and point-of-sale systems directly with banks, accounting software, and consumers. Backed by TheFactory and Innovation Norway, the company has established integrations and distribution partnerships with major Nordic financial players, including DNB and Nets. Investors may appreciate its positioning to capture value as banks and enterprises increasingly demand structured purchase data to automate corporate expense management.

q-bulderbank.summary: Bulder provides mobile-only retail banking and automated mortgages with dynamic interest rate cuts to Norwegian consumers. Launched and funded by regional savings bank Sparebanken Vest rather than venture capital, the brand scaled past 36 billion Norwegian kroner in lending volume. Investors should note it as a benchmark for automated mortgage origination, proving incumbent-backed spinouts can outcompete traditional retail lenders in user acquisition.

31fe1257-16d3-4885-b7e9-b26400bf5fc1.summary: Aprila Bank provides automated lending, credit lines, and invoice financing to small and medium-sized businesses via embedded accounting software integrations. Backed by enterprise software leader Visma and over €18 million in funding, the profitable Norwegian bank connects to more than 130,000 SMEs. Investors value its native ERP distribution and real-time data underwriting, which sharply compress customer acquisition costs and credit risk.

839f4906-b7a9-4a21-9af0-4db0249adf8b.summary: FundingPartner operates an alternative debt platform connecting Nordic real estate developers and SMEs with investor-funded loans and bonds. Backed by Schibsted and DNB, it has facilitated over NOK 4.2 billion in loans across more than 25,000 registered investors. Investors may care because tightening bank lending regulations create sustained, profitable demand for alternative debt marketplaces across the Nordic region.

q-lendonomy.summary: Lendonomy operates a gamified mobile peer-to-peer microlending app that enables young adults to lend and borrow small sums while building blockchain-backed credit histories. The startup went through Nordic accelerators, partnered with Neonomics for open banking, and raised early capital, including NOK 150,000 from Change Com. Investors may care because it captures untapped youth lending data to build portable, cross-border credit scores for credit-invisible consumers.

2f596d35-0af0-46b5-88c2-1deffb598626.summary: Two provides B2B checkout and trade credit software that enables corporate merchants to offer instant net payment terms and guaranteed settlement to business buyers. Backed by Sequoia Capital and Shine Capital, the startup has raised over €40 million and serves hundreds of European merchants. Investors value its ability to capture large transaction flows in the rapidly digitizing B2B payments market while eliminating merchant credit risk.

q-monner.summary: Monner operates a regulated crowdlending platform that provides growth and real estate loans to Norwegian SMEs by connecting them directly with retail and institutional investors. The company demonstrated strong commercial traction and was acquired by SpareBank 1 SR-Bank, subsequently rebranding its crowdlending division as Monio. Investors care because it proves viable exit pathways for Nordic alternative-lending platforms through acquisition by incumbent banking groups.

f43be408-65c5-491a-85a1-9b4dc4551df5.summary: Exabel provides an AI-driven analytics platform that turns alternative data into predictive models and actionable signals for investment managers and data vendors. Before being acquired by BattleFin in late 2024, the Oslo-based company raised over $21 million in funding. Investors should note its acquisition, which demonstrates strong strategic M&A appetite for turnkey alternative data infrastructure in institutional capital markets.

q-oblinor.summary: Oblinor operates a digital crowdfunding platform in Norway that connects property developers seeking project financing with retail investors looking to fund secured real-estate loans. Regulated under Norwegian financial authorities, the company modernized its deposit infrastructure through a partnership with open banking provider Neonomics. Investors may care because tightening bank credit for property developers drives sustained borrower demand toward alternative, asset-backed lending platforms.

q-fixrate.summary: Fixrate operates a digital marketplace connecting businesses and institutional depositors with commercial banks to place large deposits quickly at competitive rates. Backed by Innovation Norway, the company raised NOK 19.5 million from Schibsted Growth and facilitates corporate funding for multiple Norwegian banks. Investors care because digitizing traditionally rigid corporate treasury processes captures sticky, high-volume capital flows with strong marketplace network effects.

q-kron.summary: Kron provides a digital savings and pension platform that offers automated advisory and mutual fund investments directly to retail consumers. Prior to its acquisition by Storebrand in 2022, the company scaled to 67,000 retail users and NOK 7 billion in assets under management. Investors care because it proved that consumer-friendly UX can successfully capture market share from traditional Nordic wealth managers and trigger strategic exits.

q-kredd.summary: Kredd operates a digital marketplace in Norway connecting retail borrowers seeking personal loans and refinancing with peer lenders and partner banks. Backed by prominent Norwegian angels like Knut Kjær, it partnered with Ikano Bank to scale distribution amid tight consumer lending regulations. Investors may find value in its automated, open-banking credit assessment engine, which significantly accelerates loan underwriting in Norway's debt consolidation market.

q-spiff.summary: Spiff is a Norwegian fintech app offering social saving and micro-investment tools directly to retail consumers, with an initial focus on women. Backed by approximately NOK 10 million in early funding, the startup partnered with Nordea Liv to deliver goal-based pension and fund investments. Investors would care about its potential to lower acquisition costs by pairing bank distribution with collaborative, social-saving mechanics.

f50c84de-9a37-4121-bef3-aa54b3fc3157.summary: Quantfolio provides AI-driven advisory and compliance software to banks, wealth managers, and insurers to automate onboarding, suitability checks, and investment workflows. Backed by around $9.5 million in funding, its clients include major Nordic institutions like DNB and Storebrand, with over €5 billion advised through the platform. Investors may appreciate its defensible enterprise positioning, converting complex regulatory requirements into recurring B2B software revenue.

q-firi.summary: Firi provides a regulated cryptocurrency trading and custodial savings platform for retail and corporate clients across the Nordics. Backed by investors including Schibsted Ventures, the platform has grown to hundreds of thousands of users and obtained authorization under the EU’s MiCA framework. Investors may value its defensible regional leadership, anchored by seamless local banking and ID integrations that shield it from global competitors.

6cbff99f-11f2-4f4e-8cd6-fdd891b31575.summary: Folio provides an app-based business banking platform, corporate cards, and integrated expense accounting software for small and medium-sized businesses in Norway. The company has raised over $4.6 million and serves more than 31,000 businesses, powering roughly one in four new Norwegian company incorporations. Investors value its defensible entry point at company creation, which secures low customer acquisition costs and creates long-term software stickiness.

q-duneanalytics.summary: Dune Analytics provides a collaborative blockchain data platform, selling tiered API access and enterprise data services to Web3 developers, crypto protocols, and institutional investors. The Oslo-based company reached a $1 billion valuation after raising a $69.4 million Series B in 2022 and serves more than 1,000 institutional clients. Investors care because its community-generated dashboards create strong network effects, positioning Dune as Web3's default analytics layer.

29b585be-f80f-4c54-be9d-a4c17db594fb.summary: Abelee was an Oslo-based quantitative trading firm that developed adaptive, data-driven algorithmic models for foreign exchange trading. Backed by industrialist Kjell Inge Røkke and Aker, the startup accumulated over 350 million NOK in losses before initiating a controlled liquidation in 2024. Investors should care as it highlights the severe execution risks and capital intensity inherent to quantitative fintech ventures despite elite backing.

de1f80cc-3b8f-470b-b401-d56b5d1e99f4.summary: SafetyWing sells subscription-based travel and global health insurance to digital nomads, remote workers, and distributed companies. The startup has raised approximately $50 million in venture funding, including a $35 million Series B led by Kinnevik. Investors favor its established position in the remote-work economy as it expands from health insurance into a broader cross-border social safety net.

q-tjommi.summary: Tjommi provides a consumer app that scans receipts and bank transactions to automatically claim price-match refunds from retailers. It has raised over 10 million NOK from backers including Strawberry Capital and Vækstfonden while expanding across Norway and Denmark. Investors may value its hands-off open-banking savings model, though long-term growth hinges on managing merchant pushback against automated claims.

q-signicat.summary: Signicat provides digital identity verification, authentication, and electronic signature software to enterprise clients, primarily in regulated financial services. After scaling to roughly €19 million in annual revenue, the company was acquired by private equity firm Nordic Capital in 2019. Investors view it as a prime example of a Nordic compliance and identity startup expanding into a dominant pan-European market leader.

q-dreams.summary: Dreams provides behavioral savings and financial wellbeing software, offering a consumer app alongside white-label engagement banking tools for financial institutions. The company attracted over 500,000 Nordic users and raised more than €9 million before its B2B unit was acquired by Doconomy in 2023. Investors care because its cognitive science methodology effectively drives deposit growth and digital retention among younger banking customers.

q-payr.summary: Payr provides a consumer mobile app that allows users to pay bills and invoices using cards or bank accounts while comparing provider rates. The startup raised several million euros before merging with Nordic fintech group Hudya in 2019. Investors cared because Payr proved an agile non-bank could successfully unbundle traditional banking services by directly integrating Norway’s national eFaktura infrastructure.

q-strisetech.summary: Strise sells an AI-powered anti-money laundering and KYC compliance platform to financial institutions, including Nordea and Handelsbanken. The company has raised a $10.8 million Series A led by Atomico and works with a majority of top-tier Nordic banks. Investors find it compelling because intensifying regulatory enforcement makes automated AML compliance a mission-critical, non-discretionary enterprise budget priority.

q-lucidtech.summary: Lucidtech sells proprietary AI-powered OCR APIs that automate data extraction from invoices and receipts to financial institutions, software vendors, and enterprises. Backed by Finstart Nordic and StartupLab, the startup processes millions of documents annually for major clients such as DNB. Investors may care about its template-free machine learning technology and validated adoption in mission-critical, high-volume banking and accounting workflows.

5fa0685b-d6a4-4d74-97a4-f25579b3756f.summary: Boost.ai develops conversational and voice AI platforms for enterprises in heavily regulated sectors like banking, insurance, and telecommunications. Backed by Nordic Capital and reaching roughly €25 million in revenue, the company agreed to be acquired by Automation Anywhere in 2026. Investors care because its compliance-ready agents achieve 90% resolution rates in production, proving clear defensibility and strong exit potential in enterprise automation.

b4df8b5a-f24b-46b9-a25d-6f60ea9ed5f0.summary: Blockbonds develops SPENN, a blockchain-powered mobile banking app providing cost-free payments, savings, and microloans to consumers in emerging markets. It scaled to over 800,000 users across Africa and Asia before a 2021 share-swap transaction with listed SPENN Technology valued it at DKK 1.4 billion. Investors gain direct exposure to large unbanked populations by monetizing bank-partnered lending in underserved economies.

q-spoor.summary: Spoor sells computer vision and AI software to wind farm developers to track and monitor bird activity around turbines. Having raised $13.4 million, the company has deployed its solution with major energy operators, including Equinor and Vattenfall. Investors may care because strict environmental regulations make automated wildlife monitoring essential to de-risk and accelerate wind project permitting.

q-wattifevas.summary: Wattif EV provides turnkey electric vehicle destination charging infrastructure and revenue-sharing financing models to landowners, businesses, and housing cooperatives. Backed by €50 million from infrastructure fund Marguerite, the company manages more than 45,000 charge points across six European markets. Investors may value how its fully funded offering removes upfront capex for property hosts, securing sticky, long-term recurring charging revenue.

q-axeptiacreditintelligence.summary: Axeptia provides credit intelligence and risk monitoring software to businesses to manage receivables and reduce unpaid invoices. The company has raised roughly $2.6 million in seed funding and partnered with Danske Bank, which holds an equity stake and distributes the software across the Nordics. Investors may value this bank-led distribution channel, which offers institutional validation and lowers customer acquisition costs.

314e4aed-1237-4a9d-8dee-689ba8c67ec4.summary: Mobai sells privacy-preserving facial biometric verification and liveness detection software to banks, digital identity providers, and public sector organizations. The NTNU spin-off has raised $2.8 million and secured a major contract powering Norway’s national public digital ID system. Investors should note its proprietary deepfake defense and strict alignment with upcoming eIDAS 2.0 regulations, positioning it well for Europe's digital identity wallet rollout.

8af97959-0b76-4116-86cb-36b84a539de7.summary: Iris.ai provides an AI platform that helps corporate R&D teams and academic researchers search, summarize, and extract data from scientific literature and patents. The company has raised over $21 million in total funding and grants, with backing from Silverline Capital and the European Innovation Council. Investors value its domain-specific models that drastically reduce hallucinations, making generative AI reliable for high-stakes research in biotech and materials science.

q-vespa.summary: Trondheim-based Vespa sells a managed AI search and vector database platform to enterprises building large-scale retrieval, recommendation, and AI applications. Spun out of Yahoo, the company raised a $31 million Series A led by Blossom Capital and powers clients like Spotify and Perplexity. Investors should care because its underlying engine provides rare, production-proven scalability over billions of documents, differentiating it from newer vector database competitors.

q-vindai.summary: Vind AI builds software that uses artificial intelligence to optimize wind project design and cabling for renewable energy developers. The company has raised over $3.3 million, backed by Norrsken VC and DNV Ventures, and counts TotalEnergies, RWE, and Corio as customers. Investors may value the founding team's proven track record executing a similar generative-design playbook at Spacemaker, which Autodesk acquired.

cce5db61-abbb-4240-8b5e-6ed1ae48626f.summary: Simplifai sells enterprise conversational AI and automation agents that streamline claims processing, email triage, and customer inquiries for insurers and financial institutions. The company has raised $3.34 million and expanded operations across Europe and Asia. Investors may appreciate its defensible focus on compliance-heavy insurance workflows, which provide clear operational cost savings and high customer retention.

q-spacemaker.summary: Spacemaker develops cloud-based, AI-driven design software that helps architects, urban planners, and real estate developers optimize building site layouts. Before Autodesk acquired the startup for $240 million in late 2020, it had raised $25 million in venture funding. Investors care because it proved that vertical AI can compress complex multi-month planning workflows into hours, validating strong strategic acquisition demand in construction tech.

q-intelecy.summary: Intelecy provides a no-code AI platform for process manufacturing companies, allowing plant engineers to optimize production, cut emissions, and prevent downtime. The startup has raised $4.8 million from investors including Yara Growth Ventures and Investinor, serving clients like dairy producer TINE. Investors may value its ability to drive industrial decarbonization and operational savings without requiring scarce in-house data scientists.

be75b775-db43-444e-9f25-a742d1055b3a.summary: Oslo-based Visoid sells AI-powered visualization software to architects and design firms, turning 3D CAD models into photorealistic renderings in minutes while preserving underlying geometry. Backed by $3.26 million in total funding, the platform is used across 120 countries by major firms including OMA and Sweco. Investors may value its workflow-native integration, which cuts rendering times by up to 90% without generic AI hallucinations.

q-aivero.summary: Aivero provides a 2D and 3D video streaming and data management platform for computer vision researchers and industrial robotics teams. Beyond its initial $110K round, the startup has secured seed backing from Norwegian investors including StartupLab, Momentum Partners, and TRK Group. Investors may care because efficient visual data compression solves critical bandwidth bottlenecks essential for scaling vision-guided automation and real-time AI.

q-deckmatch.summary: Deckmatch sells an AI-driven API platform to venture capital firms to convert inbound pitch decks into structured CRM data and automated memos. The Oslo startup has raised roughly $4.2 million in total funding, including a $3.1 million seed round backed by Alliance VC and Luminar Ventures. Investors should note strong product validation, as every venture fund in its seed round was an active customer before investing.

q-promptshields.summary: Prompt Shields provides a self-hosted AI governance platform for enterprises, helping them block prompt injections and redact sensitive PII within their own cloud environments. The Oslo startup raised a 5 to 10 million NOK pre-seed round backed by Antler, StartupLab, and Innovation Norway. Investors may care because strict European data sovereignty and privacy regulations drive strong corporate demand for tenant-native AI safeguards.

q-factiverse.summary: Factiverse sells automated claim-detection and fact-checking software to newsrooms, financial institutions, and defense organizations to verify claims in real time. Having raised $2.4M, the company has partnered with European media outlets and joined NATO's DIANA accelerator. Investors may care because surging misinformation and generative AI hallucinations drive strong enterprise and government demand for reliable, multilingual verification tools.

28f8c0da-a4db-4474-a264-fb14afd88dda.summary: Oslo-based Altek AI sells an AI operating layer to hotels, deploying autonomous agents that integrate with property management systems to automate guest communications and booking workflows. Backed by €423K in pre-seed funding, the company has expanded to over 100 hotels across Europe. Investors may care because deep core-system integrations create strong switching costs while converting inbound guest inquiries directly into hotel revenue.

q-1xtechnologies.summary: 1X Technologies develops general-purpose humanoid robots for commercial security, logistics, and domestic consumer assistance. The company has raised over $125 million, including a $100 million Series B and backing from the OpenAI Startup Fund. Investors may find it compelling because its proprietary hardware and strategic alignment with OpenAI position it to capture early market share in embodied artificial intelligence.

q-curipod.summary: Curipod sells an AI-powered platform to K-12 educators and school districts that generates interactive lessons with real-time student feedback. Backed by Reach Capital after raising a $4.6 million seed round, it has reached over one million students globally. Investors may value its rapid organic adoption among US teachers, creating an efficient pipeline into paid district-wide SaaS contracts.

q-cradltechnologies.summary: Norway-based Cradl Technologies offers an AI-powered document data extraction platform and APIs to help mid-sized and enterprise companies automate complex document workflows. The company has raised $22 million in funding and serves major clients such as Equinor and DNB. Investors should note its built-in human-in-the-loop validation, which solves critical accuracy and compliance hurdles in enterprise automation.

fba11615-bc29-48ee-908a-8294021477f3.summary: Sonair develops patented 3D ultrasonic sensors for autonomous mobile robot manufacturers. Spun out of SINTEF, the company has raised nearly $13 million from backers including Scale Capital and Investinor while shipping to global customers. It attracts investors by cutting perception hardware costs by 50% to 80% compared to LiDAR while providing safety-certified 3D spatial awareness for human-robot collaboration.

q-sixrobotics.summary: Six Robotics develops swarm autonomy software that enables military operators to coordinate heterogeneous fleets of unmanned drones and robotic systems. Spun out of the Norwegian Defence Research Establishment, the startup raised a €12 million seed round and is already deployed with the Norwegian Armed Forces. Investors may value its hardware-agnostic platform, which addresses critical interoperability bottlenecks as NATO militaries rapidly scale drone procurement.

f9226ccd-aae0-4493-afac-1a9f09b7eb9a.summary: Remora Robotics provides autonomous underwater robots and AI monitoring that continuously clean and inspect net pens for aquaculture operators. It has raised over 240 million NOK from investors including Hatch Blue and Grieg Kapital, deploying systems with major producers like Mowi. Investors may care because replacing manual jet-washing improves fish health and biosecurity while generating recurring service revenue.

q-aviant.summary: Aviant provides autonomous drone delivery services for healthcare providers, businesses, and remote consumers, transporting medical supplies, groceries, and equipment. The startup has completed thousands of commercial flights across Scandinavia and secured over €3.3 million in seed capital and grants from backers including Luminar Ventures and Bring Ventures. Investors may value its EU flight certifications and long-range drones designed to handle harsh Nordic weather.

741c88c3-cc97-4048-9919-2d3d2263a2e7.summary: Eelume develops articulated, snake-like autonomous underwater vehicles for subsea inspection and defense, selling to offshore energy and naval defense clients. Spun out of NTNU and backed by Kongsberg Maritime and Equinor, it has raised over $4 million and secured commercial and military contracts. An investor might care because its seabed-resident design significantly cuts operational costs by eliminating the need for surface support vessels.

q-blueyerobotics.summary: Blueye Robotics develops portable underwater remotely operated vehicles and inspection software for maritime, aquaculture, and defense clients. It reached 61.1 million Norwegian kroner in 2025 revenue, has operated profitably since 2022, and supplies customers including the Norwegian Coast Guard. Investors may value its proven profitability and expanding foothold in dual-use underwater monitoring and defense inspection.

502f2d08-adc1-4184-980d-d56c98b3b598.summary: Physical Robotics develops Pi, an upper-body humanoid robot designed for precision manipulation across manufacturing, healthcare, and hazardous environments. The company is venture-backed and currently at the seed stage. Investors may care because founder Phuong Nguyen previously co-founded humanoid maker 1X Technologies, bringing proven sector pedigree to a pragmatic, legless design optimized for fine motor tasks.

76798321-83b0-4d00-bfab-f4097668b417.summary: No Isolation develops telepresence robots, primarily the AV1, sold to schools and local authorities to keep chronically ill or absent children connected to education. The Oslo-based company has raised over $7 million in funding from backers including StartupLab and deployed units across Europe. Investors might care because the company taps into dedicated public-sector education budgets with a defensible, subscription-based telepresence model.

a1fe2946-676f-4ca4-96ce-24f5b2eae813.summary: PortalOne develops a hybrid gaming platform that combines interactive video games with live broadcast-style game shows directly for mobile consumers. The company has raised over $75 million in funding, including a $60 million Series A led by Tiger Global alongside Founders Fund and Coatue. Investors may value its proprietary format merging broadcast entertainment with mobile gaming, supported by exclusive licensing partnerships with legacy brands like Atari.

q-pineleafstudio.summary: Pineleaf Studio was a Norwegian game developer that created DwarfHeim, a cooperative real-time strategy title sold to PC gamers via Steam. After securing seed capital and accumulating over 100,000 Steam wishlists, the company suffered weak post-launch sales and declared bankruptcy in January 2022. Investors should view it as a cautionary case study on the severe retention and commercial risks facing indie multiplayer games.

q-nabobil.summary: Nabobil operates a peer-to-peer car-sharing marketplace in Norway, allowing private vehicle owners to rent idle cars to nearby drivers. After raising seed funding and establishing domestic market leadership, the startup was acquired by US-based Getaround for $12 million in 2019. Investors value it as a proven model of a capital-efficient Nordic platform rapidly dominating a localized market to achieve a profitable strategic exit.

q-playmagnus.summary: Play Magnus develops chess training apps, gaming platforms, and educational content for chess players and enthusiasts worldwide. Co-founded by World Champion Magnus Carlsen, the company expanded through multiple acquisitions before being acquired by Chess.com in 2022 for approximately $83 million. Investors care because it demonstrated how athlete-led personal IP can successfully anchor and monetize a global gaming and e-learning ecosystem.

q-hyre.summary: Hyre provides an app-based, keyless car-sharing and rental platform to consumers and businesses across the Nordics. Backed by Møller Mobility Group, it operates over 2,500 vehicles and reached bottom-line profitability with roughly €34 million in 2024 revenue. Investors will care because its highly automated operations demonstrate viable unit economics in a sector where mobility operators routinely struggle to become profitable.

q-infinitemobility.summary: Infinite Mobility develops lightweight, solar-powered electric cargo bikes and tricycles for urban last-mile delivery and commercial transport. The startup expanded into Germany via the Scaleup Landing Pad program after winning the Future Hamburg Award, though specific funding figures remain undisclosed. Investors may care because its integrated solar panels generate extended daily off-grid range, lowering fleet downtime and total cost of ownership.

q-widerezero.summary: Widerøe Zero is an air mobility incubator developing commercial and operational models for zero-emission regional aviation and eVTOL services. Backed by Norwegian airline Widerøe, it has partnered with Embraer subsidiary Eve Air Mobility to prepare the deployment of up to 50 electric aircraft across Scandinavia. Investors may value its strategic position commercializing electric flight within Norway’s uniquely suited short-haul flight network.

q-vlurvolur.summary: Völur sells AI decision-support software to meat processors to optimize cutting, sorting, and production scheduling. The company has raised nearly $10 million from backers including Idékapital and Fusion Fund, serving enterprise clients such as JBS USA. Investors should note its ability to drive clear margin expansion and reduce waste across a massive, traditionally analog global industry.

q-softseaweed.summary: SoftSeaweed sells farm management software and IoT sensors to commercial seaweed growers to monitor maritime conditions, cultivation equipment, and crop growth. Its funding and commercial traction are not publicly disclosed. Investors may care because digitization and predictive yield modeling are critical to standardizing and scaling Europe's expanding sustainable seaweed aquaculture sector.

q-totalctrl.summary: TotalCtrl sells cloud-based inventory and expiry-tracking software to restaurants, grocery retailers, and food service operators to prevent food waste. The company has raised over NOK 20 million in funding alongside grants from Innovation Norway and the EU. Investors may value its measurable cost savings for margin-sensitive hospitality businesses navigating increasingly stringent European food waste regulations.

b763a50c-b1e3-48ee-95b0-d73f5e3a6dcb.summary: Flyr was an Oslo-based low-cost airline that sold domestic and European passenger flights directly to consumers through an app-first platform. After raising capital and listing on Euronext Growth Oslo in 2021, the company struggled with heavy cash burn and declared bankruptcy in February 2023. Investors should view it as a cautionary case study on the capital intensity and liquidity risks of commercial aviation.

dbbecb21-93d7-44c4-9f2d-527bccde1cca.summary: Proximar Seafood produces and sells land-based Atlantic salmon directly to Japanese distributors and retailers from its recirculating aquaculture facility near Mount Fuji. Publicly listed on Euronext Growth Oslo, the company secured tens of millions in debt and equity financing, launching commercial harvesting in 2024. Investors care because local production bypasses costly air freight while capturing strong demand in Japan’s massive raw-fish market.

790be486-c105-42b9-8e92-c9c2ab885546.summary: Poio developed a gamified learn-to-read app designed to help young children crack the reading code through play. After raising roughly $1.1 million and reaching over 100,000 Scandinavian users, the startup was acquired by Kahoot! in 2019 for $6.5 million. Investors view it as a prime example of rapid Nordic product-market fit delivering a swift strategic exit.

q-capeesh.summary: Capeesh sells an AI-powered, gamified language learning platform to corporate employers to help foreign and language-minority workers master industry-specific vocabulary. Spun out of the Norwegian University of Science and Technology, the startup has raised approximately $400,000 in seed funding. Investors may care because it addresses an underserved B2B niche, replacing costly manual workforce training with scalable, automated corporate upskilling.

q-vignita.summary: Vignita provides a B2B workplace learning and compliance platform connecting enterprises, course providers, and skilled workers for professional training. The startup has raised roughly $740,000 and served over 2,500 companies, initially gaining traction in vocational industries like construction. Investors may find it compelling for targeting acute skilled-labor shortages through automated, mandatory compliance and recurring upskilling workflows.

q-ludenso.summary: Ludenso sells an augmented reality and 3D authoring platform to educational publishers, enabling them to enrich print textbooks and digital courses with interactive media. Backed by $1M in seed funding from FERD and Kahoot! co-founders, it has secured partnerships with major publishers including Cambridge University Press and Macmillan. Investors may value how easily it digitizes legacy print catalogs without publishers needing in-house developer teams.

140bdc7a-90eb-4cc9-99b5-eda6728535e3.summary: Scrimba sells interactive coding courses and career paths to aspiring software developers. Backed by Y Combinator and Schibsted Ventures with around $2.4 million raised, the platform serves over 1.5 million users and generates profitable revenue. Investors value its proprietary format that allows learners to pause and edit instructor code directly inside videos, driving stronger engagement than conventional edtech platforms.

dce253cc-31e0-4d29-830b-373f77686ff0.summary: WeWillWrite sells a gamified, AI-supported writing platform to K-12 schools to engage students through collaborative prompts and peer feedback. The Oslo-based startup raised a €2 million seed round in late 2025 led by Skyfall and Spintop Ventures to scale U.S. classroom adoption. Investors may favor the team's track record under founder Daniel Senn, who previously created Poio and sold it to Kahoot!.

q-fairsight.summary: Fairsight sells evidence-based psychometric and bias-tracking assessment software to employers and recruitment agencies. Founded in Oslo by industry veterans Espen Skorstad and Lasse Hønsen, it integrates with platforms like Teamtailor and ReachMee, with no public funding announced. Investors may care because it addresses enterprise demand for fair, objective hiring using deeply experienced domain leadership.

170b68b1-d340-4b4e-a388-87c730f1986d.summary: We Are Learning provides an AI-powered authoring tool that enables enterprise instructional designers to quickly build interactive, 3D training scenarios compatible with any LMS. The platform is used across 50 countries by clients including Tapestry and Elkjøp, backed by a €2.3 million funding round. Investors will value the founders' proven track record, having previously created Motimate and sold it to Kahoot!.

48de6535-1cf3-4fb3-b79f-ef7e9d767a34.summary: Bookis operates an inventory-free marketplace for consumers and students to buy and sell used and new books across Norway and Sweden. Backed by investors including Schibsted, the startup raised over $6 million and grew to 500,000 users before being acquired by bookstore chain Norli. Investors value its asset-light circular commerce model that created strong marketplace network effects and delivered a proven regional exit.

q-learnlink.summary: Learnlink offers live one-on-one and small-group coding lessons using games like Minecraft and Roblox to children aged 8–15. The Oslo-based startup has taught over 4,000 students and raised approximately NOK 7.2 million in early-stage funding. Investors may find it compelling because its gamified teaching model drives strong student engagement in the growing direct-to-consumer STEM education market.

q-lingu.summary: Lingu provides a digital language-learning platform and LMS offering Norwegian and English training to corporate clients, adult immigrants, and Norwegian municipalities. Bootstrapped into a major domestic provider, it secured NOK 10 million in Norwegian government funding in 2020 to develop digital adult education tools. Investors may appreciate its defensible position within state-accredited integration programs and steady public-sector contracts.

58fa0c2a-5c64-45be-9305-c2ec2381de49.summary: Creaza sells a digital storytelling and creative learning platform to K-12 schools, enabling students to produce comics, podcasts, mind maps, and presentations. Bootstrapped with no recorded venture funding, the company is deployed across roughly 40% of schools in Norway and Sweden. Investors may value its entrenched Nordic public procurement footprint, which provides steady retention and high barriers to entry.

q-boldbooks.summary: BoldBooks operates a digital marketplace connecting independent authors directly with vetted publishing professionals, like editors and designers, to self-publish while retaining full rights. The company has raised over €1.2 million in funding and reached roughly €600,000 in annual revenue across Norway and Germany. Investors may care because it capitalizes on the creator economy by disintermediating traditional publishers through a scalable marketplace model.

q-greps.summary: GrepS provides a SaaS platform that objectively assesses and benchmarks software engineering skills for hiring employers, technical teams, and developers. The Oslo-based startup raised roughly $465,000 in seed funding and participated in TheFactory accelerator. Investors may appreciate that its skill evaluation methodology is backed by 15 years of empirical research from Simula Laboratory and the University of Oslo.

3ee757f1-15c6-4f26-aafd-eba7953589a9.summary: Pistachio sells an automated, AI-driven cybersecurity awareness and attack simulation platform to businesses to train their workforce against phishing and social engineering. The Oslo-based startup has raised over $10 million, including a $7 million Series A, and serves more than 600 corporate clients. Investors may value its zero-touch model, which requires no manual IT overhead while targeting human error, the primary cause of enterprise breaches.

q-snapmentor.summary: Snapmentor built a SaaS platform enabling universities and schools to connect students directly with teaching assistants for digital study support. Backed by StartupLab with 2 million NOK in early funding, it gained traction with institutions like NTNU and NHH before rebranding to Curipod. Investors would value its demonstrated ability to pivot into a scalable B2B enterprise model and land institutional contracts.

q-hubroeducation.summary: Hubro Education sells interactive business simulation games to universities and business schools to provide students with hands-on management training. The company scaled to hundreds of institutions across 40 countries before being acquired by global academic publisher Sage in 2023. Investors will note this demonstrates a viable strategic trade-sale exit for niche, curriculum-integrated higher education software.

8602265e-132f-42c4-8c83-156a5750d97f.summary: Wittario sells an augmented reality and GPS-powered mobile platform that combines physical movement with gamified learning for educational institutions and corporate training. The company has raised roughly $3.5 million in funding, including an oversubscribed NOK 13 million round, and serves hundreds of organizational clients. Investors may appreciate its differentiated active-learning niche and dual-market B2B model led by experienced edtech founders.

q-diwala.summary: Diwala provides a decentralized, blockchain-backed platform that enables universities, training institutions, and NGOs to issue and verify tamper-proof educational credentials. Backed by Katapult Accelerator and the EQT Foundation, the startup has piloted its solution across East Africa, including in Uganda and Kenya. Investors may appreciate its large addressable market in emerging economies by tackling credential fraud and unlocking global employment pathways for displaced talent.

q-signlab.summary: SignLab provides gamified, video-based sign language learning apps to families of deaf children, individuals, and schools. The company has expanded its curriculum to 11 sign languages across more than 12 countries, backed by early grants and over $1 million in reported revenue. Investors may note its scalable content infrastructure addressing a severely underserved global accessibility market.

q-hypatialearning.summary: Hypatia Learning provides AI-driven formative assessment tools to schools and educators to deliver automated writing feedback and track student competency. The company has secured grant funding through the Research Council of Norway and collaborates with local universities and municipalities like Halden. Investors may value its research-backed approach to classroom AI, which reduces teacher workload while meeting stringent Nordic educational and data compliance standards.

q-melodypipe.summary: MelodyPipe is a Norwegian edtech startup founded in 2020 that provides social media marketing for the education sector. Web records do not verify this specific company, so its traction and funding details remain unknown. An investor might care if it offers proprietary, cost-effective student recruitment and marketing channels for educational institutions.

q-ponebiometrics.summary: Pone Biometrics develops OFFPAD, a smart card–sized biometric hardware passkey providing passwordless authentication to enterprises, healthcare, and defense organizations. The startup has raised over 37 million Norwegian kroner (roughly $3.4 million) in private funding alongside public innovation grants. Investors may care because enterprise zero-trust mandates are accelerating demand for phishing-resistant, FIDO2-compliant hardware security backed by proprietary university patents.

a848fde5-a6db-4d84-9195-9c34ed6f57be.summary: Lace Lithography develops next-generation semiconductor patterning systems using helium atom beams instead of light, targeting advanced chip manufacturers. A spinout from the University of Bergen founded in 2023, the company raised a $40 million Series A in 2026 backed by Atomico and Microsoft M12. Investors care because atom-beam lithography bypasses the optical diffraction limits of EUV to extend Moore's Law for sub-nanometer chip fabrication.

4008c375-2152-4da8-83d1-5693d8760099.summary: Norsk Titanium manufactures 3D-printed structural titanium components using Rapid Plasma Deposition, supplying alternatives to traditional forgings to aerospace, defense, and industrial clients like Boeing and Airbus. Now publicly traded on Euronext Growth Oslo, the company has FAA-approved parts in commercial flight and generates multi-million-dollar annual revenues. Investors may value its deep regulatory and manufacturing qualification moats within bottlenecked aerospace supply chains.

313d22dd-6ec0-4e83-9c5b-e8a652130e90.summary: ScoutDI sells tethered autonomous drone systems and analysis software to maritime and heavy-industry clients for inspecting confined, GPS-denied spaces. Previously backed by Equinor Ventures and DNV Ventures, the startup agreed to a $24 million acquisition by Beam Global in late 2026. Investors value the technology because it replaces dangerous, costly manual scaffolding and human entry during mandatory industrial inspections with automated 3D mapping.

18764255-8ec5-48e9-b60f-acbe78d100e7.summary: Maritime Robotics develops autonomous uncrewed surface vessels and navigation software for defense, offshore energy, and ocean-mapping clients. Backed by a €28 million Series C round in 2026, the company generated roughly NOK 250 million in 2025 revenue. Investors benefit from surging dual-use demand as naval defense and commercial maritime operations transition from isolated trials to fleet-scale adoption.

47252293-e23e-48be-8263-0cdda647199c.summary: wheel.me sells autonomous robotic wheel modules and navigation software to manufacturing, warehousing, and healthcare operators, turning their existing carts into self-driving transport units. The company has raised tens of millions in venture funding and expanded operations across Europe and North America. An investor might care because its retrofit approach sharply lowers adoption costs for enterprises compared to purchasing dedicated autonomous mobile robots.

q-sagarobotics.summary: Saga Robotics sells Thorvald, an autonomous modular robot providing chemical-free UV-C disease control and crop analytics to commercial strawberry and vineyard growers. The company raised an $11.2 million Series C round in 2025, servicing thousands of acres across the UK and the US. Investors may value its validated commercial traction in high-value specialty agriculture, which addresses farm labor shortages while drastically reducing chemical fungicide dependence.

9b39c4c1-1900-4b78-9bdd-591078ec0ef8.summary: Hystar manufactures patented PEM electrolyzers for industrial green hydrogen producers and energy developers. Backed by over $36 million from a 2025 Series C round and a €26 million EU Innovation Fund grant, the company has deployed commercial units across Europe. Investors are drawn to its proprietary thin-membrane architecture, which significantly lowers the levelized cost of green hydrogen and enables automated gigawatt-scale manufacturing.

cdbbceb7-e667-4c33-ade6-a6507d80d05f.summary: Hive Autonomy sells retrofit AI software and sensor systems that convert existing machinery, such as forklifts and excavators, into autonomous vehicles for logistics and industrial operators. It raised a $15 million seed round in 2026 led by SuperSeed and runs live commercial deployments across Scandinavia. Investors may care because retrofitting legacy fleets avoids costly equipment replacements while directly addressing industrial labor shortages.

q-morrowbatteries.summary: Morrow Batteries manufactures sustainable lithium-iron-phosphate and cobalt-free battery cells for electric vehicles, marine vessels, and energy storage systems. Backed by over €300 million from investors including Siemens and ABB, it commenced commercial deliveries from its Norwegian gigafactory. Investors care because its low-carbon chemistries offer European industry a domestic alternative to Asian battery supply chains, despite intense capital requirements.

44995564-f924-4c0d-a13d-895d30f4ab6d.summary: Beyonder manufactures high-power, fast-charging battery cells and systems (BePowered) for heavy transport, maritime, and electrical grid operators. Backed by investors including Equinor Ventures, DSD, and Innovation Norway, it has secured over $30 million in equity and public funding. Investors may value its focus on specialized industrial applications that avoid direct competition with commodity electric vehicle battery manufacturers.

7bbf19fd-bb17-431a-a5d1-b161d4281fd1.summary: Otovo operates an online marketplace that sells turnkey rooftop solar and battery installations to residential homeowners by matching them with vetted local contractors. Listed on Euronext Oslo, the company has raised over $100 million in combined debt and equity to finance pan-European expansion. Investors track its asset-light, software-driven platform as a scalable play to consolidate Europe's fragmented residential clean energy market.

abe938df-ec7d-4a94-8efd-5f0bcd3a3e18.summary: Hydrogen Mem-Tech manufactures proprietary palladium membrane separators that extract ultra-pure hydrogen from natural gas, biogas, and ammonia for industrial and energy clients. Backed by investors including Shell Ventures, Aramco Ventures, AP Ventures, and Yara Growth Ventures, it has raised over NOK 170 million. Investors might care because its compact, SINTEF-derived technology enables cost-effective, decentralized clean hydrogen production with simultaneous carbon capture.

425ed1b8-1232-4eba-a879-a3261641972e.summary: ONiO designs ultra-low-power, battery-free microcontrollers that harvest ambient energy from light, RF, and heat, selling them to IoT hardware manufacturers for sensors, smart tracking, and retail labels. The Norwegian startup raised a €5 million Series A in 2025 led by node.vc and Maki.vc to scale chip production. Investors value its potential to eliminate battery maintenance costs and hazardous waste across billions of connected devices.

07f45b85-fc12-4911-9c54-6d0f263242c8.summary: Enode sells a unified API platform that connects distributed energy hardware—including electric vehicles, solar inverters, and home batteries—to energy suppliers, utilities, and software developers. A Y Combinator alumnus backed by Creandum, the company has raised over $17 million and integrates hundreds of device models across international markets. Investors value its potential to become the foundational data layer for grid flexibility during widespread electrification.

q-chooose.summary: CHOOOSE sells enterprise SaaS and API platforms to airlines and travel companies, enabling them to manage sustainable aviation fuel programs, track emissions, and issue carbon credits. Backed by GenZero and Shell Ventures with over $30 million in funding, it counts Delta Air Lines and British Airways among its clients. Investors care because it provides essential infrastructure to address Scope 3 emissions under tightening aviation decarbonization mandates.

ee629bed-82fb-4579-a464-4f069857258a.summary: Muybridge sells a software-defined imaging platform to sports broadcasters and live event producers, replacing heavy camera setups with compact sensor arrays and real-time computer vision. The company raised a $16 million Series A following live deployments across the NBA, NHL, and European football leagues. Investors should care because it transforms expensive physical broadcast infrastructure into scalable, high-margin software for live event production.

bf9853a3-539f-4380-babe-1eb813df04c9.summary: Ardoq sells a cloud-native enterprise architecture platform to large corporations to map complex IT landscapes, manage application dependencies, and navigate digital transformations. The company has raised over $160 million in funding, including a $125 million Series D led by EQT Growth, serving clients like Carlsberg and ExxonMobil. Investors should care because mounting IT complexity makes automated architecture software an essential, sticky enterprise category.

25ae9a4e-2539-4965-9d7b-4fac96599472.summary: Cognite sells an industrial DataOps and contextualization platform, Cognite Data Fusion, to heavy-asset enterprises across energy, utilities, and manufacturing. Backed by Accel and TCV, the company surpassed $170 million in annual revenue before Schneider Electric agreed to acquire it for $3.1 billion. Investors care because it proves that contextualizing complex operational data for industrial AI commands strong enterprise adoption and premium exits.

q-spacemakerai.summary: Spacemaker AI sells cloud-based generative design software to real estate developers, architects, and urban planners to optimize early-stage site layouts for factors like density, sunlight, and noise. Backed by a $25 million Series A from Atomico and Northzone, the company was acquired by Autodesk in 2020 for $240 million. Investors care because it proved rapid, lucrative exit potential for vertical AI targeting legacy construction and property sectors.

bf3b2824-f75e-4fad-b6ae-ea48fd4718c3.summary: Northern.tech provides over-the-air software update and device lifecycle management tools, primarily via its flagship platform Mender, to connected hardware manufacturers and enterprise IoT fleets. It serves major global clients including Siemens, Volkswagen, and Airbus, and previously secured European Union Horizon grant funding. Investors should care because stricter cybersecurity regulations, like the EU Cyber Resilience Act, increasingly mandate secure OTA patching infrastructure.

bfef764c-2c99-4871-9a33-4e21245d08c3.summary: Oncoinvent develops Radspherin, an injectable alpha-emitting radiopharmaceutical designed to eliminate residual peritoneal metastases in ovarian and colorectal cancer patients after surgery. The clinical-stage company has secured institutional backing from funds like Hadean Ventures, raising 148.5 million NOK in 2026 to advance ongoing Phase 2 trials. Investors may care because it was founded by the team behind Algeta, which Bayer acquired for 2.9 billion dollars.

q-vaccibody.summary: Vaccibody, now operating as Nykode Therapeutics, develops targeted DNA-based immunotherapies and individualized vaccines, licensing its pipeline and proprietary platform to global pharmaceutical companies. It listed on the Oslo Stock Exchange after securing major multi-hundred-million-dollar partnership agreements with Genentech and Regeneron. Investors care because its clinically validated modular platform delivers robust immune responses with proven, substantial licensing milestone potential.

q-databutton.summary: Oslo-based Databutton, rebranded as Riff, provides an AI-powered development platform that allows business teams to build and deploy custom internal tools and automations without writing code. The company has secured $21 million in total funding, including a $16 million Series A led by Northzone. Investors should care because it targets the high enterprise AI failure rate by enabling non-technical operators to create production-grade software.

q-picterus.summary: Picterus sells a CE-marked smartphone application and calibration card to healthcare providers and parents for non-invasive neonatal jaundice screening. The company has secured over €4 million in EU grants and completed multiple international clinical trials. Investors may care because its software-based approach replaces expensive specialized hardware and invasive blood tests with an easily scalable, lower-cost diagnostic tool.

9b8a443d-0d0e-472c-afcb-08f4065d5a98.summary: Disruptive Technologies sells ultra-small wireless IoT sensors to enterprise clients for smart building automation, cold-chain monitoring, and facilities management. With over 250,000 sensors deployed and $15 million in 2025 revenue, it agreed to a $130 million acquisition by Digi International in late 2026. Investors value its proprietary silicon architecture, which delivers a 15-year battery life in postage-stamp-sized hardware.

q-biome.summary: Bio-Me sells high-throughput qPCR-based microbiome profiling services and targeted diagnostic assays to pharmaceutical companies and clinical researchers. The company has raised over 1.3 million dollars in private funding alongside more than 2 million euros in public grants, while partnering with Thermo Fisher Scientific. Investors care because its platform delivers actionable diagnostic results in hours instead of weeks, enabling scalable companion diagnostics for cancer immunotherapy.

b2556446-a5fd-4af5-bf20-50b31671aad5.summary: Piscada sells a cloud-native industrial IoT and AI platform for building automation and energy optimization to commercial real estate owners and industrial operators. Backed by investors including Skagerak Capital and GK, it manages over 1,500 buildings across Northern Europe and recently signed a major framework agreement with Thon Gruppen. Investors should care because tightening ESG mandates are accelerating commercial demand for scalable, retrofittable building decarbonization software.

q-sensonomic.summary: Sensonomic sells agronomic data collection tools and predictive modeling software to commercial growers and agribusinesses to optimize crop yields and harvest planning. The company expanded commercial operations across the Iberian Peninsula following growth funding from agricultural and software investors. An investor might care because its software tackles climate volatility in high-value crops by unlocking measurable operational margins for farmers.

q-spacelab.summary: Space Lab develops reusable, sea-launched rockets and liquid propulsion systems to provide launch services for commercial and research satellite operators. Originating from the UiS Aerospace initiative, the startup raised a seed round in 2026 to advance rocket engine development and flight testing. Investors may value its strategy of leveraging Norway's offshore engineering infrastructure to build sovereign, cost-efficient European launch capabilities.

q-wastefront.summary: Wastefront uses pyrolysis to convert end-of-life tires into tire-derived oil, sustainable aviation fuel, and recovered carbon black for commodities traders, airlines, and industrial manufacturers. The company has secured an offtake agreement with Vitol, strategic funding from International Airlines Group, and is constructing a commercial processing plant in Sunderland. Investors may value its proven tier-one partnerships addressing binding sustainable aviation fuel mandates.

eaf71edb-7d82-4678-8901-37641bc3ea3c.summary: Imerso sells an AI platform that compares on-site 3D scans against BIM models to catch structural deviations for contractors and property developers. The Oslo-based company has raised venture funding from industry strategic Nemetschek Group alongside earlier seed investors. Investors may appreciate its ability to prevent costly construction rework combined with distribution access through an established global software partner.

q-igniteprocurement.summary: Ignite Procurement provides spend management and strategic procurement analytics SaaS to mid-market and enterprise businesses. The company has raised over 11 million dollars in total funding, including a 7.1 million dollar Series A led by Arkwright X. Investors may find it attractive because its cost-optimization, compliance, and carbon tracking software benefits from strong counter-cyclical enterprise demand during economic downturns.

3b7f54dd-d92c-4267-8712-3ec763cc951a.summary: N2 Applied sells on-farm plasma units to livestock farmers, enabling them to convert manure into enriched nitrogen fertilizer using air and electricity. The company has raised over €20 million in equity and EU grants, running international pilots with dairy partners like Arla. Investors care because it decentralizes the multi-billion-dollar fossil-based fertilizer industry while drastically cutting agricultural emissions.

q-unleash.summary: Unleash sells an open-source feature management platform to enterprise engineering teams to safely decouple code deployment from release. Backed by Spark Capital and One Peak, the company has raised over $51 million while serving enterprise customers like Wayfair and Lloyds Banking Group. Investors value its bottom-up open-source adoption, which positions it to capture surging enterprise demand for governance guardrails around AI-accelerated software releases.

q-callunapharma.summary: Calluna Pharma develops first-in-class monoclonal antibodies targeting innate immune pathways to treat patients with serious fibrotic and inflammatory diseases. Formed from merging Arxx Therapeutics and Oxitope Pharma, the biotech raised a €75 million Series A led by Forbion to advance its Phase 2 clinical pipeline. Investors may care about its clinical-stage lead asset addressing large unmet markets like idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis alongside seasoned institutional co-investors.

365c3bbd-c71c-41ce-a4a0-3b8a7241ba26.summary: Zelluna Immunotherapy develops allogeneic, off-the-shelf TCR-NK cell therapies targeting solid tumors for cancer patients. Backed by Takeda Ventures and public research grants, the company has progressed into early clinical testing. Investors may care because its off-the-shelf platform lowers manufacturing costs and targets solid tumors, solving key scalability and efficacy bottlenecks of traditional cell therapies.

cacac3e9-aad5-43b7-a1ef-a3ee4bd62663.summary: Hubro Therapeutics develops neoantigen-targeted peptide cancer vaccines and companion diagnostics for patients with microsatellite instability solid tumors, such as colorectal cancer. Backed by Investinor and Radforsk, the company has raised over 41 million NOK to advance clinical trials. Investors may care because it addresses high-unmet-need genetic cancer profiles led by an experienced team from Norway's established oncology ecosystem.

q-thelper.summary: Thelper develops first-in-class antibody-drug conjugates targeting tumor-specific viral antigens to treat aggressive solid cancers. The Oslo-based preclinical startup secured the first close of a €1 million seed round alongside a 16 million NOK government research grant.
