41e95b68-8de6-4299-950a-b881a7ced37d.summary: Copenhagen-based Omhu develops AI-driven teledermatology software and mobile tracking tools for patients and physicians to diagnose and monitor skin conditions. Spun out of LEO Innovation Lab in 2020, the 38-person team was acquired by clinical trial platform Medable in 2022. Investors value this precedent because it proves strong corporate acquisition demand for specialized AI diagnostic tools in healthcare.

q-perfusiontech.summary: Perfusion Tech provides image analysis software to surgical teams and hospitals for real-time tissue perfusion quantification during surgery. Its PerfusionWorks platform is CE-marked in Europe and backed by a strategic minority investment and reseller partnership with Renew Pharmaceuticals. Investors may appreciate its granted patent portfolio and hardware-agnostic design, which addresses costly surgical complications by integrating directly into existing hospital imaging equipment.

q-aiselhealth.summary: Copenhagen-based Aisel Health develops an AI-driven clinical operating system for psychiatric clinics to synthesize patient histories and automate documentation workflows. The startup raised a €1.7 million pre-seed round led by Caesar Ventures and is active across private clinics in Denmark. Investors may care because vertical workflow software built specifically for psychiatry provides strong defensibility against generic medical AI scribes while expanding strained clinical capacity.

q-alcolase.summary: Copenhagen-based Alcolase develops an oral, liposomal enzyme supplement that breaks down alcohol in the stomach before bloodstream absorption, targeting individuals with genetic alcohol intolerance. The startup raised a €1.5 million round backed by Ada Ventures and Antler to launch in Singapore and South Korea. Investors may care because it addresses an underserved market of 540 million people with proprietary enzyme delivery technology.

q-motosumo.summary: Denmark-based Motosumo sells a subscription fitness app providing live and on-demand indoor cycling classes to consumers and fitness studios. The platform uses smartphone motion sensors to track real-time workout metrics on any stationary bike and has raised over $6 million, including a Series A led by Magenta Partners. Investors may value its hardware-agnostic approach, which scales efficiently without relying on expensive proprietary exercise equipment.

q-lifelinerobotics.summary: Lifeline Robotics develops automated throat-swabbing robots for healthcare providers and public institutions to standardize pathogen sampling. Spun out of the University of Southern Denmark, the startup secured seed backing from Vækstfonden and Universal Robots co-founder Esben Østergaard. Investors may value its potential to alleviate clinical staffing shortages and eliminate cross-infection risks during high-volume diagnostic screening.

b582c11a-711e-4869-b639-75b92cc54810.summary: Copenhagen-based Enduro Genetics licenses its proprietary platform, Enduro Sense, to biopharmaceutical and industrial biomanufacturers to prevent yield loss during microbial fermentation. Spun out of the Technical University of Denmark, the company has raised €18 million in cumulative funding, including a €12 million Series A round. Investors care because it solves biomanufacturing's persistent scale-up bottleneck, reducing production costs across large addressable markets.

q-fusevectors.summary: Denmark-based Fuse Vectors develops a cell-free manufacturing platform that produces adeno-associated viral vectors for biotech and pharmaceutical gene therapy developers. The Copenhagen startup raised a €4.9 million pre-seed round in 2025 backed by HCVC and EIFO. Investors should care because its enzymatic process shortens vector production from weeks to hours, resolving gene therapy's major manufacturing bottleneck while significantly lowering costs.

q-noie.summary: Copenhagen-based Nøie sells direct-to-consumer personalized skincare products matched algorithmically to individuals suffering from chronic skin conditions such as acne, eczema, and psoriasis. Spun out of LEO Innovation Lab, the company has raised over $21 million in total funding, including a $12 million Series A led by Talis Capital. Investors may value its data-driven feedback loop, which continuously refines formulations to drive efficacy and retention in a massive dermatological market.

q-iobiotech.summary: Copenhagen-based IO Biotech develops off-the-shelf therapeutic cancer vaccines for oncology patients, targeting solid tumors such as melanoma. Backed by Novo Holdings, the company raised a €127 million Series B and secured up to €57.5 million in EIB venture debt. Investors value its dual-action platform that simultaneously destroys tumor cells and neutralizes immunosuppressive cells to complement existing checkpoint inhibitor therapies.

q-sniprbiome.summary: SNIPR Biome develops precision CRISPR-based medicines to treat multidrug-resistant bacterial infections in vulnerable clinical populations, such as cancer patients. The clinical-stage biotech has raised over $90 million in funding, including a €35 million Series B, with its lead asset in Phase 1 clinical trials. Investors care because its platform tackles antimicrobial resistance by selectively eradicating target pathogens without damaging the surrounding healthy microbiome.

f4ba54fb-7497-4d17-88c8-8bf531062d22.summary: MedTrace Pharma provides hospitals and imaging centers with an automated point-of-care system and analysis software to produce and administer oxygen-15 water radiopharmaceuticals for cardiac PET scans. Backers including Swisscanto, ATP, and the European Innovation Council have invested over €35 million to advance its Phase III clinical trials. It solves a critical logistical bottleneck by making a gold-standard, ultra-short-lived tracer practically viable in routine clinical workflows.

q-seaborgtechnologies.summary: Seaborg Technologies develops compact molten salt nuclear reactors deployed on floating power barges, targeting coastal utilities and energy-intensive industries. The company has raised nearly DKK 500 million, including a DKK 200 million round in 2025, and partners with Samsung Heavy Industries. Investors value shipyard-manufactured modular reactors for bypassing traditional onshore nuclear construction delays while meeting surging global demand for dispatchable, zero-emission baseload power.

q-galecto.summary: Copenhagen-based Galecto develops clinical-stage small-molecule therapeutics targeting galectin-3 and LOXL2 enzymes to treat severe fibrotic diseases and cancer for healthcare systems and patients. The company raised over $160 million from prominent investors including Novo Holdings, Bristol Myers Squibb, and OrbiMed prior to going public. Investors care because it targets high-unmet-need indications with orphan drug designations in multibillion-dollar fibrotic disease markets.

q-toogoodtogo.summary: Too Good To Go operates a mobile marketplace connecting consumers with restaurants, grocers, and bakeries to buy surplus food at steep discounts. Having raised over $60 million, the platform reached more than 100 million registered users and generated €194 million in 2024 revenue across 19 countries. Investors value its proven ability to build a profitable, highly scalable, network-driven marketplace directly addressing food waste reduction.

q-monta.summary: Monta sells an integrated software platform to businesses, fleet operators, and charge point owners to manage and monetize electric vehicle charging infrastructure. It has raised €130 million, including an €80 million Series B, and connects over 600,000 charge points across Europe. Investors value its asset-light software model, which captures recurring revenue from accelerating EV adoption without hardware capital expenditure.

q-zeronorth.summary: ZeroNorth sells voyage, vessel, and bunker optimization software to commercial shipping operators and owners to cut fuel costs and emissions. Backed by PSG Equity, A.P. Moller Holding, and Cargill, the company has raised over $70 million and reached nearly $40 million in ARR across 250 customers. Investors care because tightening global maritime emissions regulations drive urgent, non-discretionary enterprise demand for its proven efficiency platform.

q-agreena.summary: Agreena operates a soil carbon platform that incentivizes farmers to adopt regenerative practices, selling verified carbon credits and supply-chain decarbonization data to corporate buyers. The company has raised over €70 million in venture funding, including a €46 million Series B, and spans millions of hectares across 20 European countries. Investors value its scalable verification tech within the rapidly growing market for corporate Scope 3 emissions reduction.

q-kvasirtechnologies.summary: Kvasir Technologies develops drop-in, climate-neutral biofuels from non-edible plant biomass for the maritime shipping industry. The DTU spin-out raised a €10 million Series A from backers including Mærsk Growth and European Energy to scale commercial production. Investors may care because its fuel requires no engine or infrastructure modifications, enabling immediate adoption in a heavily regulated, hard-to-abate sector.

q-mashmakes.summary: MASH Makes uses modular pyrolysis to convert agricultural waste into biofuels for maritime shippers, alongside biochar and certified carbon removal credits. The company operates commercial facilities in India, backed by strategic investment from shipping giant Norden and €3.75 million in financing from Nefco. Investors may value its diversified revenue model directly exposed to mandatory shipping decarbonization targets.

q-arcadiaefuels.summary: Arcadia eFuels produces drop-in electro-sustainable aviation fuel and eDiesel using captured carbon dioxide and renewable electricity for airlines and heavy transport operators. The company secured a €54 million EU Innovation Fund grant and signed a 10-year offtake agreement with Uniper for its flagship Danish facility. Investors gain exposure to de-risked revenue driven by strict EU regulatory mandates requiring airlines to blend synthetic aviation fuels.

q-electricitymaps.summary: Electricity Maps provides an API offering real-time and forecasted electricity carbon intensity data to enterprises, including Google and Samsung, to optimize power consumption and carbon accounting. The company has raised €5 million from investors including Transition and Revent while covering over 200 regions globally. Investors value it as key data infrastructure enabling corporations to match flexible power demand with intermittent renewable supplies.

q-cellugy.summary: Cellugy develops EcoFLEXY, a biofabricated cellulose material sold to personal care and cosmetics brands to replace fossil-based petrochemicals and microplastics. The startup raised a €4.9 million seed round alongside an €8.1 million EU grant to scale industrial production. Investors should note that impending European regulations restricting synthetic microplastics create urgent commercial demand from major manufacturers for high-performing, bio-based alternatives.

q-hyme.summary: Hyme develops molten hydroxide salt thermal energy storage systems that convert renewable electricity into high-temperature industrial heat and steam for utilities and manufacturers. Spun out of Seaborg Technologies, it secured over €17 million in blended funding and grants while operating an industrial pilot in Esbjerg. Investors care because industrial heat decarbonization represents a massive addressable market, though severe capital intensity creates high commercialization risk.

q-dynelectro.summary: Dynelectro develops modular solid-oxide electrolyser units that produce clean hydrogen for heavy industries and synthetic fuel producers. It has raised 11 million euros in equity alongside 9 million euros in grants, backed by EIFO, Vsquared Ventures, and Yara Growth Ventures. Investors may care because its patented technology extends electrolyser lifespan from two to ten years while dynamically adapting to intermittent renewable power.

q-algiecel.summary: Algiecel builds modular photobioreactors that convert captured industrial CO2 into microalgae-based protein and omega-3 ingredients for pet food, cosmetics, and animal feed producers. The company raised 8 million euros in 2024 and expanded to an industrial-scale production facility at Novonesis’s Kalundborg site. Investors may value its ability to replace strained, volatile marine fish-oil supply chains with scalable, circular bio-based alternatives.

q-klimate.summary: Klimate sells a carbon asset management platform and vetted carbon removal portfolios to corporate clients aiming for net-zero emissions. The Copenhagen startup raised a 3.5 million euro seed round backed by Eneco Ventures and EIFO, contracting roughly 200,000 tonnes of carbon removal. Investors may care because corporate buyers are shifting budgets away from low-quality offsets toward verifiable, durable removals to satisfy regulators and avoid greenwashing.

q-again.summary: Again uses bacterial gas fermentation to convert industrial CO2 emissions into green base chemicals, selling them to industrial manufacturers and chemical distributors. Spun out of DTU, the company has raised around $100 million in equity and grants, including a $43 million Series A co-led by GV. Investors care because it targets the multi-trillion-dollar petrochemical market with cost-competitive, drop-in replacements validated by commercial offtake agreements.

q-greenmobility.summary: GreenMobility operates an app-based, free-floating electric car-sharing service for urban commuters and businesses. Listed on Nasdaq Copenhagen, the company manages an operational fleet of around 1,400 electric vehicles across Danish cities. Investors might care because its established mobility-as-a-service model directly capitalizes on municipal decarbonization mandates and the accelerating shift away from private vehicle ownership.

q-stiesdalgroup.summary: Stiesdal develops and sells floating offshore wind foundations, modular hydrogen electrolyzers, and carbon-negative pyrolysis systems to energy and industrial operators. The company has raised over $120 million from backers including Andel and Chr. Augustinus Fabrikker, with commercial units and test systems already operational. Investors value its modular, mass-manufacturing approach to capital-intensive climate infrastructure, led by wind-power pioneer Henrik Stiesdal.

q-stiesdalhydrogen.summary: Stiesdal Hydrogen manufactures standardized, modular alkaline electrolysers for renewable energy developers and industrial Power-to-X operators. Backed by parent company Stiesdal Group—which has raised over $120 million—it has deployed multi-megawatt commercial units with customers like European Energy. Investors may care about its modular manufacturing approach, which achieves system capital costs roughly half the European market average to make green hydrogen economically viable.

q-rodiniageneration.summary: Rodinia Generation provides automated on-demand microfactory technology, combining proprietary software and hardware, to apparel manufacturers and fashion brands. The company has raised over €7 million from investors including Climentum Capital, EIFO, and Vitamin°C to scale operations into Portugal. Investors may care because its zero-water, localized production model directly reduces inventory overproduction risk while cutting lead times and carbon emissions.

q-spirii.summary: Spirii sells turnkey electric vehicle charging management software and apps to businesses, fleet operators, and charging network owners. After raising funding from Nordic Alpha Partners, the company expanded across 18 European markets and was acquired by Edenred in 2024. Investors care because it shows that hardware-agnostic software platforms in the EV charging ecosystem can scale rapidly to a strategic corporate exit.

q-flexecharge.summary: Flexecharge provides a hardware-agnostic load and energy management software platform for electric vehicle charge point operators. It has raised over €5 million from investors including Eneco Ventures and EnBW New Ventures, while partnering with regional networks like Recharge. An investor may care because the technology mitigates grid capacity bottlenecks, allowing operators to monetize charging flexibility without infrastructure delays.

q-donkeyrepublic.summary: Donkey Republic provides turnkey bike-sharing systems—including smart-locked bicycles and software—to European municipalities, public transport authorities, and urban riders. Listed on Nasdaq First North Copenhagen, the company operates across more than 60 cities and recently raised a €10 million private placement alongside multi-million-euro green debt facilities. Investors may appreciate its city-contracted partnership model, which offers more predictable, subsidized revenue and regulatory stability than typical venture-backed micromobility operators.

q-everfuel.summary: Everfuel produces and distributes green hydrogen and operates refueling infrastructure for heavy industry and commercial transport fleets. The company brought its 20 MW HySynergy production facility online and has secured major funding, including a €245 million German government grant. Investors may care because it is positioned as a key infrastructure provider in Europe's emerging cross-border hydrogen supply corridors.

q-blueworldtechnologies.summary: Blue World Technologies manufactures high-temperature methanol fuel cell systems to replace combustion engines and diesel generators, primarily targeting maritime and heavy-duty transport operators. The company has raised over €60 million, securing backing from strategic investors including Maersk Growth, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, and Deutz AG. Investors care because it directly tackles hard-to-abate shipping emissions using scalable technology adapted to liquid green fuels.

q-nitrovolt.summary: NitroVolt builds containerized electrochemical units that allow farmers to produce green ammonia on-site using air, water, and renewable power. Spun out of the Technical University of Denmark, the startup has raised over €4.2 million, including a €3.5 million seed round backed by EQT Foundation and EIFO. Investors care because it decarbonizes high-emission fertilizer manufacturing while protecting farms from volatile global supply chains.

q-utiligize.summary: Utiligize provides SaaS asset-management and predictive forecasting software to electricity distribution system operators and utilities to optimize grid capacity and maintenance. The company has raised approximately €2 million from backers including Eviny Ventures and Aura, and serves more than 20 European utilities. Rapid electrification is driving urgent demand for grid-planning software capable of significantly cutting costly grid reinforcement capital expenditures.

q-exowave.summary: Exowave sells modular wave energy converters for renewable electricity and zero-emission desalination to offshore wind operators and coastal communities. It has demonstrated offshore prototypes in the North Sea and secured over 14 million Danish kroner in EUDP grant funding with partner Semco Maritime. Investors may value its ability to integrate with offshore wind farms, boosting power yield while addressing coastal freshwater scarcity.

q-lun.summary: Lun develops workflow software for tradespeople to streamline heat calculations and heat pump installation planning. The startup raised a €10.3 million seed round backed by Norrsken VC, Partech, and Lowercarbon Capital. Investors may care because removing administrative overhead for installers solves a critical labor bottleneck in Europe's transition away from fossil-fueled residential heating.

q-osenergy.summary: Copenhagen-based os.energy operates consumer brand Osmund, selling cost-price electricity alongside subscription-based smart energy management software to residential households. The company recently raised a €1 million pre-seed round led by PSV Tech to scale its platform. Investors may appreciate its asset-light approach, which automates utility administration with AI while capturing recurring subscription revenue from smart home energy flexibility.

q-biophero.summary: BioPhero develops biologically fermented insect pheromones as eco-friendly alternatives to chemical insecticides for the agricultural sector. Spun out from the Technical University of Denmark, the startup raised a $17 million Series A before being acquired by FMC Corporation in 2022 for approximately $200 million. Investors view it as a landmark exit proving synthetic biology can profitably displace conventional chemical pesticides at commercial scale.

q-blueenergy.summary: Blue Energy develops shipyard-prefabricated, modular nuclear power plants to deliver zero-emission baseload electricity to utilities and data centers. It has raised a $45 million Series A round and signed a letter of intent with a data center provider. Investors are drawn to its off-site assembly model, which significantly slashes construction delays and capital costs to capitalize on booming clean-power demand.

q-faunaphotonics.summary: FaunaPhotonics develops optical sensors and AI software that monitor insect activity and biodiversity in real time for farmers, forestry managers, and corporate landholders. Backed by North Ventures and EU grant funding, the Danish company has collaborated with industry players such as John Deere. Investors may care because stringent CSRD and biodiversity reporting regulations are driving commercial demand for automated, verifiable ecological monitoring.

q-nordetect.summary: Nordetect provides portable lab-on-a-chip hardware and software to commercial growers and indoor farmers for rapid, on-site chemical and nutrient analysis of water and soil. The startup has raised approximately $1.75 million in funding from backers including SOSV, Rockstart, and Luminate NY. Investors may find it compelling because replacing multi-day laboratory testing with instant data helps growers optimize fertilizer use, cut costs, and increase crop yields.

q-eivee.summary: EIVEE provides carbon accounting and sustainable procurement software to help enterprise clients measure and report Scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions across their supply chains. The startup raised a €4 million seed round from SEED Capital in 2022 and was acquired by Swedish carbon platform Normative in November 2024. Investors should note this quick exit as evidence of strong M&A liquidity driven by European sustainability reporting regulations.

q-unibio.summary: Unibio licenses gas-fermentation technology and sells UniProtein, a methane-derived protein, to animal feed producers and agribusinesses. The company has raised over $70 million, including a major round from Saudi Industrial Investment Group to build large-scale production facilities. Investors care because the technology decouples protein production from arable land and overfishing while turning industrial gas emissions into feed.

q-tomorrow.summary: Now operating as Electricity Maps, Tomorrow sells real-time and forecasted grid carbon-intensity data and APIs to enterprises such as Google for carbon-aware operations. The company has raised over €5 million in funding from investors including Transition and Revent. Investors value its position as an established data standard powering granular, round-the-clock corporate carbon accounting and energy load-shifting.

q-co2hero.summary: CO2HERO sells a gamified SaaS platform that helps corporate employers engage workforces in sustainable daily habits and track Scope 3 emissions. Largely bootstrapped by angel investor Susanne Brønnum, the company has logged over 400,000 app downloads and participated in Denmark’s Accelerace program. Investors may value its potential to capture growing corporate spend as enterprise ESG compliance and Scope 3 reporting mandates intensify.

q-cogo.summary: Cogo provides a shared mobility aggregator app to consumers, letting them compare and book eco-friendly shared rides across hundreds of operators. It raised €1.9 million from backers including PreSeed Ventures and scaled to over one million users before Mayten acquired its assets in 2024 following bankruptcy. Investors care because it highlights the strong user demand for consolidating fragmented urban micro-mobility alongside the challenge of monetizing consumer transit platforms.

q-mate.summary: Copenhagen-based MATE designs and sells stylish, foldable electric bicycles to urban consumers and business partners worldwide to promote zero-emission commuting. After initially launching via record-breaking crowdfunding campaigns, the company has raised over $40 million in funding from backers including Nordic Eye and Marcy Venture Partners. Investors may care about its proven ability to combine sustainable micromobility hardware with high-margin lifestyle branding across international markets.

q-sharksolution.summary: Shark Solutions recycles laminated windshield and architectural glass into sustainable polyvinyl butyral polymers and glass cullet, which it sells to paint, coating, and flooring manufacturers. The Danish company operates processing plants across Europe and the United States and is backed by Circularity Capital and AXA IM Alts. Investors may care because its proprietary recycling process replaces virgin petrochemical binders at commercial industrial scale.

q-rematch.summary: Re-Match recycles worn artificial turf for sports clubs and municipalities, selling the reclaimed rubber, sand, and plastic fibers to industrial manufacturers. Operating commercial factories in Denmark and the Netherlands, it secured over €30 million in funding backed by Verdane and Nordic Alpha Partners. Investors may care because its patented technology offers a circular solution to tightening regulations against landfilling composite sports plastics.

q-agrain.summary: Agrain upcycles brewer's spent grains into high-protein, high-fiber flours and food ingredients sold to commercial bakeries and food manufacturers. The company has raised over DKK 26 million from investors including EIFO, Collateral Good Ventures, and Planetary Impact Ventures. Investors may value its ability to tap abundant brewery waste to create scalable, land-free ingredients that reduce carbon emissions and resource use for food producers.

q-scanmetals.summary: Scanmetals uses proprietary dry-sorting technology to recover non-ferrous metals from incinerator bottom ash, selling the refined materials to global smelters and foundries. Operating across Denmark, Germany, the UK, and Spain, it generates over $100 million in revenue with backing from Kirk Kapital and Polaris. Investors should care because it pairs profitable circular-economy scale with rising industrial demand for low-carbon recycled metals.

q-sempercycle.summary: SemperCycle develops patented gasification technology that converts non-recyclable, mixed plastic waste into liquid chemical feedstocks like methanol for plastics and chemical manufacturers. Backed by The Footprint Firm and Danish public grants, the company operates a pilot demonstration facility at DTU Risø. Investors may value its ability to profitably process contaminated plastics that mechanical recycling cannot handle, addressing large commodity chemical markets.

q-aquaporin.summary: Aquaporin manufactures energy-efficient, biomimetic water filtration membranes and purification systems for residential consumers and industrial clients in sectors like textiles and food processing. Listed on Nasdaq Copenhagen, the company generates tens of millions in DKK annually and raised DKK 172 million through a 2024 rights issue. Investors value its patented natural-protein technology, which significantly cuts the energy required for industrial wastewater treatment and reuse.

q-stiesdalskyclean.summary: Stiesdal SkyClean sells industrial pyrolysis systems to the agriculture and energy sectors, converting biomass waste into biochar and renewable fuels. Part of Stiesdal Group, which has raised over $170 million, the venture has built and commissioned a flagship 20 MW plant in Denmark. Investors may care because the technology creates dual revenue streams by combining durable carbon removal credits with green energy production.

q-hybirdenergy.summary: Hybird Energy sells intelligent electrical panels and an AI-driven software platform to commercial and industrial facilities to automate energy reduction. It has raised €2.4 million in seed funding and is live across 15 Danish sites, cutting power use by an average of 30%. Investors may care because upgrading legacy switchboards pairs proprietary hardware with recurring software to address building efficiency and power grid strain.

q-perplant.summary: Perplant sells tractor-mounted AI camera sensors to farmers, enabling real-time, precision spot-spraying of herbicides and fertilizers. The company has raised over €1 million in funding and secured a commercial partnership with tractor manufacturer Valtra to offer factory-fitted units. Investors may care because its plug-and-play retrofit lowers chemical costs and usage, offering farmers rapid payback amid tightening European environmental regulations.

q-visibuilt.summary: Visibuilt produces mycelium-based bio-binders to replace fossil-derived bitumen and cement for asphalt manufacturers and infrastructure developers. The company has raised over €3.3 million in funding and partnered with industry players like Munck Asfalt for real-world testing. Investors may value its potential to decarbonize heavy construction materials while drastically reducing manufacturing energy consumption.

q-acodyne.summary: Acodyne develops high-speed, autonomous electric eVTOL cargo aircraft for defence, offshore energy, and remote logistics operators. The startup has raised a €2.5 million pre-seed round backed by Gungnir Capital, PSV Hafnium, and Denmark's EIFO. Investors may care because its ducted-fan system targets lucrative dual-use markets by replacing expensive manned helicopters with lower-cost, zero-emission heavy-lift freight.

q-veo.summary: Veo sells portable AI-driven cameras and an automated video analytics subscription platform to amateur, youth, and professional sports teams worldwide. It has raised over $110 million in funding and is used by tens of thousands of clubs across more than 100 countries. Investors might care because it successfully pairs proprietary hardware with recurring SaaS revenue in an underserved, high-volume grassroots sports market.

q-supwiz.summary: SupWiz sells omnichannel conversational AI software, including chatbots and automated ticket-routing tools, to enterprise and public-sector customer service teams. Founded by University of Copenhagen computer science researchers, the company raised roughly $2.9 million in funding before being acquired by Norwegian cloud contact center provider Puzzel in 2024. Investors value it as evidence that capital-efficient Nordic research spinouts can secure profitable trade exits.

q-neurons.summary: Neurons sells AI-driven neuromarketing software that predicts consumer attention and emotional response on visual assets to enterprise brands and creative agencies. The Danish company has raised over €6 million in seed funding from investors including Fairpoint Capital and counts Google and IKEA among its clients. An investor might care because it replaces slow, expensive focus groups with instant, data-backed creative pre-testing.

q-evaxionbiotech.summary: Evaxion Biotech licenses AI-discovered immunotherapies and personalized vaccines for cancer and infectious diseases to global pharmaceutical partners. Listed on Nasdaq, the company demonstrated commercial traction by out-licensing an AI-designed vaccine candidate to MSD in a partnership worth up to $592 million. Investors may care because its proprietary platform successfully translates computational models into clinically validated assets with proven Big Pharma demand.

q-abzu.summary: Abzu develops explainable AI software, powered by its proprietary symbolic regression engine QLattice, to help pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies accelerate drug discovery. The company has raised over €9 million from backers such as Inventure and the EIC Accelerator, gaining commercial traction with large pharmaceutical clients. Investors care because its transparent, white-box approach resolves critical interpretability and regulatory hurdles in life sciences that black-box AI cannot address.

q-uizard.summary: Copenhagen-based Uizard sells an AI-powered design and prototyping platform to non-designers, product teams, and enterprises, converting sketches and text prompts into functional UI mockups. The company raised over $18 million, including a $15 million Series A led by Insight Partners, before being acquired by Miro in 2024. Investors value its proven exit track record and category leadership in democratizing software interface design through generative AI.

q-goautonomous.summary: Go Autonomous provides an AI SaaS platform that extracts unstructured quote and order data from incoming emails and inputs it into ERP systems for B2B manufacturers and distributors. The company raised a $10.3 million Series A backed by Octopus Ventures and counts enterprise clients like Danfoss and Grundfos. Investors may value its ability to automate high-volume commerce workflows without forcing buyers to change habits.

q-modlai.summary: Copenhagen-based modl.ai sells AI-powered quality assurance and playtesting software to video game developers, deploying adaptive bots to automate testing and balance gameplay. The company has raised an €8.5 million Series A round co-led by Griffin Gaming Partners and Microsoft’s M12. Investors may find it compelling because it automates a notoriously labor-intensive, multi-billion-dollar bottleneck in game development, significantly accelerating production cycles.

q-jabbr.summary: Jabbr develops DeepStrike, a computer-vision platform providing automated video production, real-time fight analytics, and objective scoring to combat sports broadcasters, promotions, and gyms. The startup has raised a $5 million seed round backed by Buckley Ventures and Alexis Ohanian’s Seven Seven Six, already debuting its metrics on networks like DAZN. Investors may value its ability to digitize subjective officiating and drastically reduce broadcast production costs.

q-colossyan.summary: Colossyan provides a generative AI platform that enables enterprise learning and development teams to generate multilingual, avatar-led training videos from text. The company has raised over $27 million, including a $22 million Series A led by Lakestar, and serves clients like BMW and Vodafone. Investors note its ability to disrupt corporate training by cutting traditional video production costs and turnaround time by up to 80%.

q-dreamdata.summary: Dreamdata sells an AI-powered revenue attribution and activation platform to B2B marketing teams to track complex, multi-touch customer journeys. The Copenhagen-based company has raised 67 million dollars in total funding, including a 55 million dollar Series B, and serves thousands of business clients. Investors care because it resolves B2B data fragmentation by directly tying marketing spend to closed revenue, establishing a vital operating system for go-to-market teams.

q-pandektes.summary: Pandektes sells an AI-powered legal research platform that indexes case law and legislation for law firms, corporate legal teams, and public institutions. The Copenhagen-based startup has raised €17.5 million in total funding, including a €13.5 million Series A, and serves more than 500 organizations across Europe. Investors may care about its roughly two-thirds trial-to-paid conversion rate and potential to unseat entrenched legacy legal publishers.

q-valuer.summary: Valuer sells an AI-driven platform that matches corporations, accelerators, and investors with early-stage startups and emerging technologies. Having raised over $20 million, including a 2021 Copenhagen First North IPO before delisting in 2023, it has served clients like Microsoft and Danske Bank. Investors may care because it automates deal intelligence, significantly reducing the time enterprises spend sourcing M&A targets and innovation partners.

q-tracksights.summary: Copenhagen-based TrackSights sells an AI-powered data platform to car dealerships and fleet operators, providing automated vehicle valuations and real-time market analytics to optimize pricing and inventory. The company secured a €1 million pre-seed round led by Maki.vc in early 2025. Investors may find it compelling because it replaces manual, spreadsheet-based valuation processes across a massive, fragmented European automotive market.

q-dixa.summary: Dixa sells an AI-powered customer engagement platform that unifies email, voice, chat, and messaging for consumer-facing brands. The Copenhagen-based company has raised over $155 million in funding, anchored by a $105 million Series C led by General Atlantic. Investors may care because it challenges legacy help desks with intelligent routing and sentiment analysis in a high-value customer support software market.

q-rebloom.summary: ReBloom develops an AI-driven platform that matches private and institutional investors with secondary shares in late-stage, pre-IPO companies. The Copenhagen-based startup raised a €400,000 pre-seed round in early 2025 to expand its infrastructure. Investors may care because prolonged IPO delays are driving massive demand for private market liquidity, which ReBloom captures by automating previously opaque, manual secondary transactions.

q-spaak.summary: Spaak develops an AI platform that automates legislative tracking, policy research, and memo drafting for public affairs teams, enterprises, and NGOs. The company has onboarded more than 40 organizations and raised a €1.5 million pre-seed round led by node.vc and J12 Ventures. Investors may value its targeted vertical AI model disrupting high-cost political consultancy as it expands into broader European regulatory markets.

q-viggo.summary: Viggo provides an all-electric ride-hailing service and ultra-fast EV charging network to urban consumers and businesses in Denmark. After raising nearly $6 million and expanding to 300 vehicles serving 450,000 users, it was acquired by Bolt in 2025. Investors note its proven ability to achieve scale and secure a trade exit within tightly regulated European mobility markets.

f6503720-7a2e-4df2-baaa-75b19702713e.summary: Spiri developed an on-demand urban carpooling service using custom lightweight electric vehicles, offering free travel to drivers who picked up paying commuters along their route. The startup unveiled a prototype vehicle in 2016 and secured millions of euros in early funding. Investors were drawn to its attempt to replace paid drivers with commuter-driven pooling to radically reduce the operating costs of urban transit.

599dd852-ebc8-4ec4-8aad-9f203a378be1.summary: Copenhagen-based Driversnote sells automated mileage-tracking and tax-reporting software to self-employed professionals and businesses managing employee reimbursements. Largely bootstrapped and profitable, the company scaled past €10 million in ARR and over two million users before partnering with VIA equity. Investors may appreciate its exceptional capital efficiency and dependable SaaS retention driven by an essential, recurring compliance need.

c28c78bd-79da-4875-85a1-de008a7152dd.summary: Simplyture provides barrier-free, ticketless parking management and enforcement software using automated license plate recognition to parking operators and facility owners. Having expanded operations across the Nordics and the UK, the company was acquired by Norway-based Autopay Technologies in 2025. Investors value it as an example of successful commercialization and exit viability in asset-light, automated urban mobility infrastructure.

q-ooono.summary: OOONO sells screen-free hardware devices and a companion app to everyday drivers and commercial fleets, providing real-time alerts for speed cameras and road hazards. The company has raised nearly $4 million in total funding and scaled annual revenues past 580 million DKK with millions of active units deployed across Europe. Investors may value its self-reinforcing community network effects paired with proven commercial viability in consumer mobility hardware.

q-matebike.summary: MATE.Bike designs and sells stylish foldable electric bicycles to urban commuters and lifestyle consumers globally. After raising over $40 million from venture backers and selling more than 24,000 bikes across 80 countries, the company completed a financial restructuring to stabilize operations. Investors might care because its luxury collaborations validate high brand equity, though micromobility hardware margins require disciplined execution.

q-holoautonomousmobilityas.summary: Holo provides turnkey deployment, fleet management software, and operations for autonomous passenger and freight vehicles to public transit authorities and municipalities. It has logged over 100,000 autonomous kilometers across 11 routes in five Nordic and Baltic countries, with backing from automotive group AMAG. Investors may value its hard-to-replicate regulatory approvals and real-world operational data bridging autonomous vehicle technology into public transit.

q-tjekvik.summary: Tjekvik sells digital self-service kiosks and mobile check-in software to automotive dealership service departments to automate key drop-offs and aftersales upselling. Deployed across more than 30 countries, the platform processes millions of annual check-ins and secured a majority investment from Standout Capital in 2025. Investors value its ability to modernize sticky dealership workflows while directly boosting high-margin dealer revenues through automated add-on sales.

q-simplefeast.summary: Simple Feast provided organic, plant-based meal-kit subscription boxes directly to consumers across Denmark, Sweden, and the US. Before declaring bankruptcy and liquidating in September 2022, the startup raised over $80 million from backers including Balderton Capital and Kinnevik. Investors view it as a cautionary case study on the steep capital intensity and unit economics challenges inherent to direct-to-consumer food delivery.

q-matrfoods.summary: MATR Foods produces clean-label, fungi-fermented meat alternatives from organic Nordic crops, selling to foodservice chains and grocery retailers. The company secured a €20 million Series A co-led by Novo Holdings as part of a €40 million package to scale a 4,000-tonne production facility. Investors should note its solid-state fermentation eliminates ultra-processed additives, positioning it to capture demand where traditional meat substitutes struggle.

67152851-51ea-4d61-9f3c-ac32dfedca29.summary: Ecofleet provides GPS-based fleet management and connected vehicle software to commercial businesses and enterprise fleets across the Nordic and Baltic regions. Previously backed by Vækstfonden and Ambient Sound Investments, it scaled to over 80,000 subscribers before being acquired by Fleet Complete in 2018. Investors care because it validated a clear regional consolidation and M&A exit path for Nordic B2B mobility telematics platforms.

q-yourlocal.summary: YourLocal operates a mobile marketplace connecting grocery stores, bakeries, and restaurants with local consumers to sell surplus food nearing expiration at discounted prices. Backed by Seed Capital, it raised over DKK 3 million and reached over 70,000 users across 500 partner stores. Investors may value its practical approach to monetizing retail shrinkage amid accelerating consumer demand and regulatory pressure to reduce food waste.

q-21stbio.summary: 21st.BIO provides a precision fermentation scaling platform and strain development services to food, materials, and agricultural companies producing recombinant proteins. Backed by Novo Holdings, it has raised over $100 million through Series C and secured US regulatory approval for its animal-free dairy protein. Investors may value its technology licensing partnership with Novonesis, which de-risks commercial-scale bioproduction and accelerates time-to-market.

q-temptyfoods.summary: Tempty Foods produces mycelium-based meat alternatives, selling to foodservice providers and major retailers including Coop Denmark and 7-Eleven. The startup raised 5.2 million DKK in seed funding backed by EIFO and business angel networks to support Nordic expansion. Investors may value its proven retail traction and asset-light manufacturing model within the growing alternative protein market.

q-myco4food.summary: Myco4Food develops AI-controlled solid-state fermentation systems to produce mycoprotein ingredients from industrial side streams like brewer’s spent grain for food manufacturers. The Aalborg University spinout is backed by the BioInnovation Institute and has secured Danish InnoFounder support alongside a €1.2 million consortium grant. Investors may value its automated bioreactors, which solve a key scalability bottleneck in commercializing cost-competitive, circular proteins.

f7c34c6d-5bbf-4819-97a6-56a99c74f618.summary: Chromologics develops precision fermentation-derived natural food colorants, primarily its flagship red dye Natu.Red, targeting global food and beverage manufacturers. Spun out from the Technical University of Denmark, the company has raised roughly 20 million euros from backers including Novo Holdings and EIFO. Investors should note tightening regulatory restrictions on synthetic dyes, which drive strong market demand for clean-label, cost-competitive replacements.

q-nutrumami.summary: Rebranded as SUMM Ingredients, the Danish startup sells multifunctional fermented protein powders to B2B food manufacturers to enhance flavor and replace synthetic texturizers. Following an initial €450K pre-seed, it raised €1.7 million from investors including EIFO, BoxOne, Kost Capital, and Planetary Impact Ventures. Investors may care because its clean-label ingredient directly solves the persistent taste and texture limitations holding back broader plant-based food adoption.

q-naturembioscience.summary: NatuRem Bioscience develops high-protein microalgae ingredients, primarily Chlorella vulgaris, for food manufacturers. The company secured non-dilutive backing through a DKK 750,000 Danish Food Innovation consortium grant and collaborates with Danish research institutions. Investors may value that its microalgae strain sidesteps EU Novel Food regulatory approvals, significantly accelerating commercial time-to-market in the sustainable protein sector.

q-biosyntia.summary: Biosyntia uses precision fermentation to manufacture bio-based active ingredients, such as natural biotin, selling B2B to food, supplement, and cosmetics producers. It has raised over 17 million euros from backers including Sofinnova Partners and Novo Seeds, alongside commercial partnerships with Wacker and Givaudan. An investor may value its proprietary technology replacing petrochemical-reliant ingredient synthesis with sustainable alternatives across massive global markets.

q-evodiabio.summary: EvodiaBio produces precision-fermented natural aroma molecules, primarily hop substitutes branded as Yops, sold to breweries and beverage manufacturers. The company has raised approximately $21 million, securing backing from RA Capital and Symrise while reaching industrial-scale production. Investors may care because climate change increasingly threatens agricultural hop harvests, driving commercial demand for reliable, sustainable flavor alternatives.

q-aligamicroalgae.summary: Aliga Microalgae sells fermented microalgae ingredients, including a proprietary neutral-tasting white Chlorella, to global food, feed, and dietary supplement manufacturers. The company scaled production by acquiring a Dutch industrial facility in 2022 and supplies commercial clients across 24 countries. Investors may value its patented white Chlorella, which removes algae’s typical taste and color barriers for mainstream plant-based formulations.

5af9309a-4a9f-4b10-b25d-9715999b25a0.summary: OrderYOYO provides white-label online ordering, point-of-sale, and marketing software directly to independent takeaway restaurants across Europe. The company went public on Nasdaq First North Denmark in 2021, expanded annual recurring revenue past 290 million DKK, and agreed to be taken private by Pollen Street Capital. Investors are drawn to its sticky SaaS model that helps restaurants bypass high third-party delivery portal commissions and retain customer ownership.

q-kaffebueno.summary: Kaffe Bueno sells upcycled functional ingredients, such as natural oils and fibers derived from spent coffee grounds, to cosmetics, nutraceutical, and food manufacturers. It has raised around $7.5M, including a €6.2M Series A led by biorefinery group Borregaard, and commercializes products with partners like Givaudan. Investors may note its validated biorefinery platform, which addresses growing enterprise demand for circular, lower-emission raw materials.

q-quickorder.summary: Quickorder provides an all-in-one restaurant management platform—combining point of sale, online ordering, kitchen displays, and table booking—to food and hospitality venues. The company raised approximately $16 million through Series B funding and expanded across four Nordic markets before joining Shopbox in 2023. Investors care because consolidating fragmented restaurant workflows drives sticky recurring software revenues and regional M&A interest.

q-superb.summary: Superb sells an all-in-one guest experience management platform to restaurants, combining table reservations, guest profiles, ticketing, and marketing tools. The Copenhagen-based company has raised over €13 million in funding, including a €12 million Series A round led by Kinnevik. Investors may care because replacing fragmented point solutions with a unified data layer creates strong software stickiness across an underserved hospitality sector.

q-fresto.summary: Fresto sells an all-in-one cloud SaaS platform to restaurants and hospitality operators, unifying point-of-sale, table reservations, payments, and kitchen management. The company raised seed funding from Nordic Makers and the Danish Growth Fund. Investors may care because replacing fragmented third-party hospitality tools with a single core operating system creates high customer retention and software stickiness.

q-barma.summary: Barma provides an all-in-one operations, onboarding, and e-learning platform to restaurants, bars, and hotels. The Denmark-based startup has secured seed funding and serves hospitality clients across several European markets. Investors may find it compelling because high frontline turnover in hospitality creates strong demand for integrated software that automates staff training and internal communications.

q-cordulus.summary: Cordulus provides hardware-enabled SaaS that pairs proprietary weather stations with AI-driven hyperlocal forecasts for farmers and agribusinesses. It operates thousands of stations across over 20 countries and raised a €6.8 million Series A backed by Delphinus Venture Capital and Rockstart. Investors may value its proprietary sensor network, which generates defensible real-time data to expand its AI models into energy trading.

q-kanpla.summary: Kanpla sells an operating and ordering SaaS platform to contract caterers and institutional canteens to streamline lunch services and cut food waste. The Danish startup raised an €8 million Series A led by henQ and serves thousands of canteens across ten European countries. Investors may value its strong expansion in a large, underserved catering market adapting to hybrid workplace demand.

q-noahs.summary: Denmark-based Noahs provides modular kitchens, operating software, and digital food brands to convenience stores, gas stations, and supermarkets to operate multi-brand food hubs. The company raised €1.9 million at a €6.5 million valuation and has expanded across retail networks including Q8. Investors may care because its plug-and-play model enables legacy retailers to capture high-margin digital food revenue with minimal capital expenditure.

q-takeoutgroup.summary: Takeout Group provides white-label ordering, dispatching, and aggregation software to restaurants to help them manage deliveries and retain customer data. The Danish company raised roughly $2.4 million in total funding, including a Series A round arranged by US Capital Global. Investors value platforms that disintermediate high-commission food delivery marketplaces, creating recurring SaaS revenue tied to direct restaurant orders.

q-plantjammer.summary: Plant Jammer provides an AI recipe assistant for consumers alongside B2B SaaS tools for food brands and retailers to minimize household food waste. The company has engaged over 300,000 users and secured €4 million in funding from investors including Miele, Dr. Oetker, and Vækstfonden. Investors may care because strategic appliance partnerships position its culinary software to power next-generation connected smart kitchens.

442fb241-1579-4f37-b45e-74bfdcf711bb.summary: Seasony develops autonomous mobile robots, including its flagship robot Watney, to automate material handling and crop monitoring for vertical farming operators. The company raised a €1.5 million funding round led by North Ventures and the Export and Investment Fund of Denmark. Investors may care because it addresses vertical farming’s primary profitability barrier by cutting labor costs with flexible automation instead of expensive fixed machinery.

q-bemakers.summary: Bemakers provides a distribution platform that helps beverage producers sell directly to European businesses and consumers while automating customs, VAT, and excise duty compliance. The Copenhagen startup raised a €3.5 million seed round in 2024 and serves over 200 brands. Investors may value its ability to simplify Europe's fragmented, heavily regulated alcohol market into a scalable infrastructure model.

fc1c1c80-5477-43d1-9df8-f8f0ef2f90e1.summary: Denmark-based eSmiley provides SaaS solutions for food safety compliance, digital self-inspection, and food waste tracking to professional kitchens, restaurants, and canteens. Backed by VIA equity, the platform operates across more than 20 countries and serves over 17,000 kitchens. Investors should note how mandatory food hygiene regulations paired with corporate waste-reduction mandates drive high switching costs and sticky recurring subscription revenue.

q-ishspirits.summary: ISH Spirits produces alcohol-free spirits, wines, and premixed cocktails sold to consumers, retailers, and hospitality venues across more than 15 countries. The company has raised over $9 million in funding, including a €5 million strategic investment from Nordic beverage group Anora. Investors may care because it holds established commercial distribution within the rapidly expanding global non-alcoholic adult beverage market.

f432dbb4-5d0b-48d5-9ef8-754baecfdf48.summary: eloomi develops a learning management and people development platform that helps mid-market and enterprise employers manage onboarding, compliance, and employee training. The startup raised approximately $78.7 million and scaled to over 850 global customers before being acquired by Dayforce in 2024. Investors value its trajectory as proof that specialized Nordic B2B SaaS platforms can successfully scale and achieve trade-sale exits to major global enterprises.

5c32f3c7-fc21-411e-b579-ab9d33c00d25.summary: Shape Robotics sells modular educational robots and turnkey STEAM classroom solutions to primary and secondary schools worldwide. Listed on Nasdaq First North after raising roughly $25 million, the company generated DKK 302 million in 2024 revenue with positive EBITDA. Investors may care because it demonstrates rare, profitable scaling by securing large-scale public education and digitization procurement contracts.

1622da84-ff4a-4eb1-ae3a-f34d4e404cea.summary: Copenhagen-based Famly sells an all-in-one SaaS platform to early childhood education providers, streamlining administrative tasks, invoicing, and parent communication. The company has raised around $22 million, led by Susquehanna Growth Equity, and serves thousands of childcare centers across Europe and the US. Investors care because mission-critical vertical SaaS in fragmented, historically analog markets yields high retention and strong switching costs.

d36ad914-2dce-4c15-b2a6-bb9224109c8f.summary: Copenhagen-based Airtame sells a hardware-enabled SaaS platform for wireless screen sharing, hybrid conferencing, and digital signage to schools and enterprises. Having raised roughly $22 million from backers including PreSeed Ventures and EIFO, it serves tens of thousands of organizations worldwide. Investors value its transition from one-off hardware sales into high-margin recurring software revenue across global education and corporate markets.

q-lms365.summary: LMS365, now rebranded as Zensai, sells an employee learning and talent development platform integrated natively into Microsoft 365 and Teams for enterprises. The company raised a $20 million Series A in 2023 and serves millions of users across 60-plus countries. Investors are drawn to its native Microsoft integration, which reduces adoption friction and taps directly into Microsoft’s massive enterprise footprint.

q-alice.summary: Alice provides an AI-powered study platform that converts uploaded course materials into personalized study guides and exam preparation for students. Backed by Y Combinator and Cherry Ventures, the Danish startup raised €4.2 million in 2025 and serves over 250,000 users. Investors may care because its strong organic traction and viral student adoption demonstrate scalable demand in AI-driven education.

q-lixtechnologies.summary: Denmark-based Lix Technologies provides an all-in-one digital textbook and study platform for university students, integrating course literature with interactive tools like note-taking and search. The company has raised approximately $8 million in funding to expand its catalog and digital reader. Investors may care because its platform addresses the expensive, fragmented academic publishing market through a scalable digital distribution model.

q-peergradeio.summary: Peergrade provides a software platform to schools and universities that automates anonymous, rubric-based peer review of student assignments. Backed by Y Combinator and Nordic Makers, it raised $1.9 million in seed funding before evolving into Eduflow and being acquired by Multiverse in 2023. Investors value its ability to eliminate educator grading bottlenecks while driving student engagement through collaborative, formative assessment.

7e249878-5e48-480a-97d1-1dcd83c737e2.summary: Eduflow sells a collaborative learning management platform to businesses and educational institutions to deliver interactive, peer-led training courses. Backed by Y Combinator and seed capital, the startup was acquired by UK edtech unicorn Multiverse in May 2023. Investors care because it proved how specialized social-learning software can achieve an M&A exit by solving engagement bottlenecks for larger corporate training platforms.

5022b971-7a02-41ed-93ec-ae003c8ae9fe.summary: Diplomasafe provides a SaaS platform for universities and training organizations to issue secure, tamper-proof digital certificates and badges, serving institutions such as the Technical University of Denmark. The company has raised approximately €1 million from investors including Ugly Duckling Ventures and KMD Venture. Investors may value the founding team’s national digital identity background and its alignment with EU-wide digital credential standards.

c2b11c3e-d279-4452-a391-5a2fd238aaa2.summary: SynergyXR provides a no-code extended reality platform that enables manufacturing and industrial companies to create virtual training, onboarding, and remote collaboration environments. Backed by Kvanted and Innovestor, the Danish startup has raised over $5 million to expand across Europe and North America. Investors may value its potential to capture enterprise SaaS revenue as heavy industries cut training costs without requiring in-house 3D developers.

q-skidos.summary: Copenhagen-based Skidos sells subscription access to a suite of educational mobile games teaching math, reading, and logic to parents of children aged 3–10. Backed by Seed Capital and PSV, the startup has raised approximately $1.2M in early-stage funding. Investors may value its recurring consumer revenue model, which embeds curriculum-aligned learning into popular licensed entertainment IP to drive retention.

q-brain.summary: Brain+ sells digital therapeutics and cognitive stimulation therapy software to healthcare providers, therapists, and patients living with dementia. Having initially raised seed financing, the Danish company later listed on Nasdaq First North Denmark to fund expansion across Europe. Investors may care because it targets an expanding, high-unmet-need dementia market using scalable, non-pharmacological digital interventions.

q-edulab.summary: EduLab sells adaptive digital math learning platforms, including flagship product MatematikFessor, via subscription to K-12 schools, teachers, and parents. The company raised over $7 million in funding, including Series A backing from Vækstfonden, and reached over 70% of Danish primary schools before being acquired by educational publisher Alinea. Investors care about its proven domestic market dominance and demonstrated strategic exit potential to legacy publishers.

q-opinoma.summary: Opinoma provides an evaluation and feedback software platform to secondary and vocational schools, linking student surveys directly with teacher professional development. Backed by a 2023 seed round, the startup serves more than 25 educational institutions in Denmark. Investors may note its sticky, recurring SaaS model driven by standardizing statutory educational measurement and evaluation workflows.

88ad8dfc-37c8-4306-83d8-8e3eefa9b6c3.summary: Swap Language provides digital and live language training to companies to help international employees integrate and communicate locally. The Aarhus-based startup raised a €2 million seed round in 2023 backed by Sparkmind.vc and Mediahuis Ventures, serving enterprise clients like Bestseller and Trustpilot. Investors may value its enterprise-focused model, which directly tackles the costly challenge of foreign talent retention across European markets.

q-maneno.summary: Maneno provides a subscription-based, gamified reading app for children aged 4 to 12, offering interactive ebooks to families and schools. Having raised approximately $866,000 in seed funding, the platform has reached over 25,000 children across the Nordics and the UK. Investors may care because its dual consumer and classroom model addresses early literacy and dyslexia with strong gamified retention features.

q-wilgoartificialintelligence.summary: Wilgo Artificial Intelligence develops an AI-driven personalized tutoring and exam-prep app for secondary school students. The company raised a €6 million seed round in 2025 backed by investors including Daphni. An investor might care because its gamified, motivation-focused learning model addresses student disengagement and demonstrated rapid early adoption across thousands of schools.

q-justlearn.summary: Just Learn operates an online marketplace connecting language learners worldwide with verified native tutors for one-on-one lessons. The Danish company has raised approximately $130,000 in pre-seed funding and reported over $360,000 in platform sales. Investors may appreciate its capital-efficient marketplace model in digital education, though it faces stiff competition from entrenched global tutoring platforms.

q-kuborobotics.summary: KUBO Robotics sells screen-free educational robots and physical coding tiles to primary schools to teach programming to children aged four to ten. The company has secured over 53 million Danish kroner in funding to support expansion across international markets. Investors may value its patented tactile learning system, which addresses growing early STEM curriculum mandates without requiring screens or tablets.

q-hopspots.summary: Hopspots develops interactive physical sensor tiles paired with digital educational games, selling to primary schools, preschools, and special care institutions. The company secured early backing from Borean Innovation and expanded through resellers across several European markets after appearing on Denmark's version of Shark Tank. Investors may care because its kinesthetic hardware-software platform addresses growing institutional demand for screen-balanced, movement-based learning in public education.

q-lululab.summary: Lulu Lab creates serious edtech games teaching reproductive health, menstrual hygiene, and sexual rights, distributing primarily through NGOs and international aid organizations. Traction includes grant backing from the British Council and field deployments across East and West Africa with partners like Save the Children. Impact-focused investors may value its institutional distribution pipeline, though its pathway to high-margin commercial software revenue remains unproven.

ff28de19-c2f1-4c23-b840-3523e1e70d46.summary: Moxso provides an AI-powered human risk intelligence platform that delivers automated phishing simulations and adaptive security training to enterprise workforces. The Copenhagen-based startup raised a $5.5 million seed round led by Seed Capital after tripling revenue across the Nordics. Investors are attracted to its shift from static compliance checkboxes toward measurable, automated behavioral defense in the expanding human-risk cybersecurity market.

q-onecolorgames.summary: Copenhagen-based One Color Games develops mobile educational math and logic games, such as its flagship app Matix, targeted directly at students, children, and adults. The studio has raised no disclosed external funding, with Matix surpassing 500,000 Google Play downloads. Investors may care about its proven ability to generate organic consumer adoption in gamified STEM learning on lean resources.

1788c089-dea8-4990-9f8b-297ab367614b.summary: Heyhack sells continuous automated penetration testing software to software development teams to secure web applications and APIs. After securing a €1.5 million pre-seed round led by PreSeed Ventures in 2022, the startup was acquired by F5 in 2024. Investors value this model because it replaces costly, episodic security consulting with scalable continuous compliance, demonstrating strong strategic acquisition appeal.

q-muninnai.summary: Muninn sells AI-powered network detection and response software to enterprises and public entities protecting critical digital infrastructure. The company raised a €2.5 million seed round from Luminar Ventures and PreSeed Ventures before being acquired by Logpoint in October 2024. Investors should note its founding team of MIT-trained and Danish intelligence cyber experts, which validated commercial demand and delivered a clear exit.

8890acdd-b887-4d42-a053-a52937fe38bc.summary: Improsec provides penetration testing, incident response, and cyber defence consulting to corporate and public sector clients. The company was acquired in 2020 by IT Relation and subsequently integrated into the Nordic IT group itm8. Investors will view it as an exit benchmark demonstrating how specialized Nordic security consultancies can be acquired and consolidated into larger private-equity-backed IT platforms.

q-sparrowquantum.summary: Sparrow Quantum manufactures deterministic on-chip single-photon sources for optical quantum computing companies and secure communication providers. Spun out from the Niels Bohr Institute, it closed a €27.5 million Series A in December 2025, with hardware already adopted by European commercial partners. It offers investors pure-play component exposure to the critical building blocks required for scalable, room-temperature quantum systems.

q-onrobot.summary: OnRobot manufactures plug-and-produce end-of-arm tooling, such as robotic grippers, sensors, and software, for industrial automation and manufacturing clients. The Odense-based company has raised over $150 million in funding from backers including Summit Partners and the European Investment Bank. Investors are drawn to its brand-agnostic hardware ecosystem and proven leadership under former Universal Robots CEO Enrico Krog Iversen.

q-2021ai.summary: 2021.AI provides its GRACE platform to enterprises and public-sector organizations, enabling them to develop, govern, and secure AI models responsibly. Having raised around $15 million, including a €3.6 million bridge round backed by DNV Ventures, it serves international clients across multiple regulated sectors. Investors may care because its governance tools position the company to capture enterprise demand driven by compliance mandates like the EU AI Act.

q-blueoceanrobotics.summary: Blue Ocean Robotics develops autonomous mobile service robots, primarily UV-C disinfection systems, for healthcare facilities and pharmaceutical manufacturers such as AstraZeneca. The company raised over $80 million from backers including A.P. Møller Holding before being acquired by 3C Groups in 2025. Investors track it as a benchmark for navigating capital-intensive hardware scaling and restructuring toward strategic exits in regulated sectors.

q-atlant3d.summary: ATLANT 3D sells atomic-scale additive manufacturing equipment and microfabrication services to semiconductor, aerospace, and research organizations. The company has raised roughly $35M across Series A rounds and works with over 50 partners, including NASA and STMicroelectronics. An investor might care because its single-step direct printing bypasses complex cleanroom fabrication, significantly accelerating device development while reducing material waste by up to 90%.

q-munatherapeutics.summary: Muna Therapeutics develops oral small-molecule drugs targeting neuroinflammation and microglial function for patients with neurodegenerative disorders like Alzheimer's and Parkinson's. Backed by roughly $79 million from investors including Novo Holdings and Sofinnova, the company recently reported positive Phase 1 clinical results for its lead candidate. Investors care because its oral, disease-modifying approach addresses massive unmet clinical needs with high pharmaceutical acquisition potential.

q-portchain.summary: Portchain sells AI-driven berth alignment and resource planning software to container terminals and shipping lines. The startup raised over $12 million and expanded its network to more than 200 terminals representing 40% of global container capacity before being acquired by StormGeo. Investors care because connecting shipping carriers and ports unlocks strong two-sided network effects while significantly cutting costly congestion delays and vessel emissions.

q-globetracker.summary: Globe Tracker sells IoT telematics devices and tracking software to maritime carriers and logistics operators for real-time monitoring of refrigerated and dry cargo containers. The Danish company has raised over $11 million in funding and generates roughly $15 million in annual revenue. Investors may value its entrenched position in perishable cold-chain logistics, which commands high switching costs and sticky subscription revenue from global shipping fleets.

q-arkynstudios.summary: Arkyn Studios sells mobile and desktop apps providing real-time SAP data integration for field maintenance teams at asset-heavy enterprises. Backed by Trifork Labs, the startup has raised approximately $10 million and serves enterprise customers including Energy Transfer with over 8,000 technicians. An investor might care because it drives high user adoption on top of complex legacy systems, securing sticky, high-value enterprise contracts.

333355df-cca1-48a4-aa98-7da6341e4ac8.summary: Podimo offers a subscription-based audio streaming platform, selling premium, local-language podcasts and audiobooks directly to consumers across Europe and Latin America. The Copenhagen-based company has raised over €200 million from backers including 83North and Highland Europe while expanding across multiple international markets. Investors may care because its hyper-local content strategy and creator revenue-share model provide defensibility against global streaming giants like Spotify.

q-nornorm.summary: NORNORM provides circular furniture-as-a-service subscriptions, maintenance, and workspace design to businesses rather than selling office furniture outright. Backed by Inter IKEA and Verdane, the company has raised over €160 million and operates across 17 European countries serving clients like Netflix and Miro. Investors care about its predictable recurring revenue that directly benefits from corporate ESG mandates and demand for hybrid-work flexibility.

881b4850-4a7c-489e-9dd5-8081fd42f0e8.summary: SOUNDBOKS designs durable, high-volume portable Bluetooth speakers built for festivals, outdoor gatherings, and party enthusiasts. The Y Combinator alumnus has raised around $9 million in venture funding and scaled sales across Europe and North America, generating tens of millions in annual revenue. Investors may appreciate its strong brand community and demonstrated ability to defend a high-margin niche within consumer audio.

q-finematter.summary: Finematter operates a curated e-commerce marketplace connecting consumers directly with independent fine jewellery designers, alongside services to repair, remodel, and recycle precious pieces. The Danish-founded startup has raised approximately $2.85 million in seed funding from Heartcore Capital and prominent angel investors. Investors may care because it introduces a circular business model and centralized digital distribution to a fragmented, high-margin luxury jewellery industry.

64b0e2cc-9724-4953-acd9-a6a3e2cdecd8.summary: Organic Basics is a Danish direct-to-consumer brand selling ethically sourced underwear, activewear, and everyday essentials for men and women. After raising venture capital from investors like Nordic Eye and Eutopia, the company faced liquidity issues and was acquired by Delta Galil in 2022. Investors care because its trajectory illustrates both high consumer demand for certified sustainable goods and the capital-intensive risks of scaling physical inventory.

q-sonofatailor.summary: Son of a Tailor sells made-to-measure apparel essentials directly to consumers online using proprietary sizing algorithms and on-demand manufacturing. The company has raised over $7 million in funding, backed by investors including eEquity, and serves an international customer base. Investors are drawn to its zero-inventory model, which eliminates unsold stock, cuts textile waste, and lowers typical e-commerce return rates.

d2bfc5bb-90bd-45c6-bbc9-735cb348b912.summary: LifeX operates fully furnished, serviced co-living apartments on flexible terms for relocating young professionals and corporate expats. The company has raised over $18 million from investors including Cherry Ventures and Founders, expanding to hundreds of rooms across major European hubs. Investors may value its asset-light operator model, which captures steady rental demand driven by chronic housing shortages in prime European cities.

q-worksome.summary: Worksome provides an external workforce management platform that helps businesses source, contract, and pay freelancers compliantly across more than 150 countries.
