The company has raised over $2 million in seed funding, led by Superhero Capital. Investors may value its purely software-driven approach, which enables remote physiological screening without requiring specialized medical hardware.

eed17506-c220-438d-9f6f-b91086d2510d.summary: Tallinn-based Salesforge provides an AI-powered sales execution platform and email infrastructure software to B2B teams seeking personalized, high-deliverability outbound outreach. The company raised a $500,000 pre-seed round in 2024 after reaching $1 million in ARR across more than 800 clients with a lean team. Investors may value its demonstrated capital efficiency in automating labor-heavy sales workflows amid tightening email deliverability standards.

q-teletactica.summary: Teletactica builds jamming-resistant communication systems and hardware for military drones and robotic platforms operating in electronic warfare environments. The Estonian-Ukrainian startup raised $1.5 million in funding and secured an R&D contract from Estonia’s Ministry of Defence. Investors should care because its technology is already combat-tested in Ukraine, providing rare operational validation for European defense procurement.

q-laxiai.summary: Tallinn-based Laxi.ai sells an AI customer support and shopping assistant to online merchants across storefronts like Shopify and BigCommerce. Founded in 2024 and part of the Startupbootcamp portfolio, the company has announced no outside venture funding to date. Investors may appreciate that it pairs support automation with catalog-aware product recommendations, turning a customer service cost center into a direct revenue driver.

3fc18fd1-d404-4b59-a629-383a987445c9.summary: Fleetbrains sells AI-driven inventory and pricing intelligence software to automotive dealerships and fleet operators to optimize vehicle turnover. The Estonian startup raised €800,000 from Icebreaker.vc in 2025 and has analyzed roughly 300,000 vehicle transactions. Investors may care because its ex-Bolt leadership directly targets costly used-vehicle overstock and depreciation risks across a massive European market.

q-phageenergy.summary: Phage.Energy provides an AI-driven virtual power plant platform to renewable energy operators, battery storage owners, and compute providers to optimize real-time asset dispatching. Founded in 2025, the Tallinn-based company remains unfunded and has released a mobile dispatch application. Investors may care because it addresses clean grid curtailment by dynamically matching surplus renewable electricity with flexible AI compute demand.

q-clevonnowindigoeurope.summary: Estonia-based indiGO Europe (formerly Clevon) develops fully electric, autonomous delivery vehicles for retail and logistics clients, including DHL, DPD, and Colruyt Group. Having completed commercial public-road deployments across Europe and raised over €5 million, the startup was acquired by US-based indiGO Technologies. Investors value its rare regulatory approval for driverless public-road operation and its demonstrated potential to slash last-mile delivery costs.

q-auvetech.summary: Auve Tech manufactures Level 4 autonomous electric shuttles and fleet management software for airports, municipalities, and commercial campuses. The company holds Level 4 regulatory approval in Japan, operates driverless airside shuttles at Tallinn Airport, and has received millions in state R&D grants. Investors may favor its focus on geofenced routes, which enables near-term commercial adoption and labor savings through remote multi-vehicle supervision.

q-schbotrobotics.summary: Schbot Robotics designs and sells autonomous vacuum and window-cleaning robots to consumers and businesses through retail outlets and e-commerce. The company sells over 4,000 units annually across Estonia and is beginning exports to the United States without disclosed venture funding. Investors might value its proven local sales traction, though breaking into the highly competitive US consumer robotics market presents steep distribution challenges.

q-rollorobotics.summary: Rollo Robotics provides autonomous, self-balancing monowheel security robots via a robotics-as-a-service model to industrial facilities and critical infrastructure operators. The startup raised a €3.7M pre-seed round led by FoodLabs and Prototype to deploy pilot programs. Backed by Cleveron co-founder Arno Kütt, the company offers strong upside by using a single-wheel architecture that significantly reduces hardware costs and mechanical complexity compared to multi-wheel patrol robots.

1186f299-654d-4694-a53e-82a35d11d381.summary: Robot Muralist sells spray-painting robots and mural-printing services to commercial property owners, public art initiatives, and outdoor advertising clients. The Tartu-based startup completed projects across Europe and the United States before being dissolved. Investors were interested in its potential to automate large-scale facade painting without scaffolding, drastically reducing labor costs and execution time.

q-basetrack.summary: BaseTracK sells fuel-economy systems and autonomous driving software to commercial freight and logistics fleet operators. The company has raised over $5 million in funding while expanding deployments across Europe and the Middle East. Investors may value its ability to immediately curb fuel expenses—which represent roughly a third of fleet operational costs—while creating an adoption path toward driverless transport.

q-spacedrip.summary: Spacedrip sells automated, modular wastewater treatment and recycling systems to industrial facilities and defense organizations. The company has raised €1.5 million and deployed over 20 systems across four countries, including field tests with the US Army. Investors may value its dual-use commercial and defense appeal for addressing global freshwater scarcity through decentralized, off-grid infrastructure.

q-yanstarstudio.summary: Yanstar Studio develops and monetizes mobile casual games directly to consumers, primarily through its flagship mobile social-deduction title Undercover: Word Party Game via ads and in-app purchases. The bootstrapped studio generates several hundred thousand euros in annual revenue without recorded institutional funding. Investors might value its ability to run lean, profitable operations supported by organic player adoption in group gaming.

q-coolbet.summary: Coolbet operates an online gambling platform offering sports betting, casino games, and poker directly to consumers across Europe, Latin America, and Canada. The company scaled to hundreds of thousands of active users before being acquired by GAN Limited for $175.9 million in 2021. Investors care because it demonstrates how Baltic teams can build proprietary gaming technology to achieve large-scale strategic exits in regulated global markets.

q-unsinkablerobotics.summary: Unsinkable Robotics developed modular autonomous underwater drones for maritime operators and offshore energy companies to inspect submerged infrastructure and conduct dangerous tasks like mine detection. Backed by incubators like ESA BIC Estonia and a €20,000 Prototron grant, the startup struggled to achieve commercial scale and dissolved in 2024. Investors should note both the rising demand for offshore infrastructure monitoring and the high capital intensity plaguing early-stage marine hardware.

q-fracturelabs.summary: Fracture Labs develops Decimated, an open-world survival game with a blockchain-based economy for gamers, while licensing its multiplayer backend infrastructure to other game studios. The company has raised over $8 million from backers including Spartan Group and Huobi Ventures, alongside an Epic MegaGrant. Investors may appreciate its dual-revenue potential spanning consumer Web3 gaming and reusable B2B development tooling.

q-plummygames.summary: Plummy Games develops and publishes casual free-to-play mobile titles for global consumers, anchored by its flagship game Star Merge. While external funding is not publicly disclosed, the studio has grown to roughly 90 employees across Estonia and Moldova. Investors may care about its proven data-driven execution in the lucrative casual merge category paired with a cost-efficient regional talent base.

q-chimeras.summary: Tallinn-based Chimeras develops a free-to-play, play-to-earn mobile game featuring NFT creature breeding, battles, and virtual land plots for mobile and Web3 gamers. The company raised a $2 million seed round in October 2021. Investors may find value in its strategy of combining conventional casual mobile gaming mechanics with blockchain tokenomics to attract broader audiences.

1f80324b-1955-4fd1-99cb-7bac7da4ecf0.summary: Scorestars built a basketball fan engagement platform offering digital card collectibles and fantasy games directly to sports fans. It secured partnerships with multiple European basketball leagues and raised €725,000 in seed funding led by Trind VC and Startup Wise Guys. Investors cared because it offered a gamified channel to engage and monetize younger demographics, though the company subsequently ceased operations.

q-cardalonia.summary: Tallinn-based Cardalonia develops a play-to-earn strategy game and metaverse on the Cardano blockchain, selling virtual land and digital assets to web3 gamers. The company secured $420,000 in pre-seed funding in 2022. Investors may care because it positioned itself as an early mover targeting gaming and virtual land monetization within the Cardano ecosystem.

q-cryptofightclub.summary: Tallinn-based Crypto Fight Club develops an NFT-enabled combat game where Web3 gamers buy, battle, and rent out digital prizefighters using native tokens. The startup raised roughly $2.8 million in seed funding from backers including Shima Capital and AU21 Capital. Investors took interest in its monetization model, which integrated on-chain NFT character lending and staking directly into competitive gameplay.

q-legendsofelysium.summary: Tallinn-based Legends of Elysium develops a free-to-play digital card and board strategy game, selling virtual items and an NFT trading marketplace to competitive gamers. The studio launched the title across major PC storefronts and raised undisclosed financing, including a 2024 token round backed by Token Ventures. Investors may care about its potential to bridge traditional strategy gameplay with Web3 digital asset ownership.

q-amgaeymetaversegaming.summary: AEY Metaverse Gaming (AMG DAO) operates a Web3 gaming guild and player onboarding platform that connects gamers to blockchain games and manages in-game NFT assets. The Estonian company secured seed funding from Oktogon Ventures in 2022. Investors may care about its ability to aggregate player communities and capture revenue from user adoption across emerging Web3 and play-to-earn gaming economies.

q-longstage.summary: Longstage develops gamification software for corporate HR teams, embedding game mechanics into recruitment, onboarding, and employee training. Initially launched with blockchain-gaming roots and backed by Estonia’s Tehnopol incubator, the company generates modest five-figure revenue with no major disclosed venture funding. Investors may care because applying gaming dynamics to enterprise HR directly addresses costly pain points like candidate drop-off and employee turnover.

q-originalgames.summary: Original Games develops casual mobile titles, such as Merge Inn, targeting a global consumer audience. Backed by Play Ventures, the studio has raised $6 million in funding and achieved millions of downloads across its releases. An investor might care because the company is staffed by experienced talent from tier-one mobile gaming studios, including Rovio, EA, and Wooga.

q-spinblade.summary: Spinblade develops a Web3 play-to-earn battle game where players collect, customize, and duel digital spinning tops. The studio raised a $250,000 angel round in 2022 to fund development and community growth. Investors may care about its potential to monetize nostalgic, Beyblade-inspired competitive mechanics through blockchain-based asset ownership.

q-ultra.summary: Ultra operates a blockchain-powered PC game distribution platform and marketplace for developers and gamers, enabling game publishing and digital asset trading. The Tallinn-based startup has raised €10.8 million in funding, led by NOIA Capital. Investors may care because it challenges dominant storefronts like Steam by offering studios better revenue cuts and players secondary resale rights.

318f3395-b57a-4745-be60-2a4fb3a21429.summary: NFTPort sells API infrastructure to developers and gaming studios to mint, manage, and verify NFTs across blockchains without writing smart contracts. It raised a $26 million Series A co-led by Atomico and Taavet+Sten, reporting adoption by over 30,000 developer teams. Investors value its turnkey picks-and-shovels model that lowers the technical and cost barriers to building Web3 applications.

q-passportgg.summary: Passport.GG provides identity and competition management infrastructure to esports federations, tournament organizers, universities, and gaming leagues. While its external funding and traction metrics remain undisclosed, the platform provides player verification, ranking systems, and event APIs. Investors may care because it operates as a sticky B2B infrastructure layer solving player authentication, integrity, and fragmentation across grassroots esports communities.

q-cricketstarmanager.summary: Estonia-based CS Games develops Cricket Star Manager, a mobile sports management simulation game aimed at global cricket enthusiasts and mobile gamers. Built in collaboration with Swedish studio Gold Town Games, the project launched on Android, though external funding details remain undisclosed. An investor might care because it targets the largely untapped sports management market for cricket, which commands an audience of over two billion global fans.

q-sisutech.summary: SisuTech develops a cloud-native iGaming and sports betting platform, licensing software to operators while running proprietary consumer brands like ReSpin. The Tallinn-based company has secured approximately €21 million in funding, including a €14 million round led by Level Up Entertainment. Investors are drawn to the founding team's proven track record, led by Jan Svendsen, whose previous gaming exits topped €240 million.

q-flyfeed.summary: FlyFeed produces insect-based protein, oils, and fertilizers from black soldier flies, supplying pet food and animal feed manufacturers. The company raised $3 million in seed funding and secured over €10 million in off-take pre-contracts for its industrial production facility in Vietnam. Investors may value its circular model, which offers a scalable alternative to increasingly volatile and resource-intensive soy and fishmeal supplies.

q-ioaio.summary: ÄIO develops fermentation-derived fats and oils from agricultural and forestry byproducts, selling them to food and cosmetics manufacturers to replace palm oil and animal fats. Backed by roughly $7.8 million from investors like Voima Ventures, the startup has scaled production to demonstration batches. Investors may value its ability to address surging corporate demand driven by strict European Union anti-deforestation regulations.

q-biteful.summary: Biteful provides a digital ordering platform and B2B storefront that connects food and beverage suppliers with restaurants, cafes, and bars. Backed by accelerator Startup Wise Guys, the Estonian startup has raised seed financing. Investors may value its potential to build network effects by replacing fragmented, manual phone and email orders across the hospitality supply chain.

q-yummy.summary: Yummy delivers chef-designed meal kits with pre-portioned fresh ingredients directly to consumers across Estonia and Central Europe. Originating as Clean Kitchen, the startup has raised €3.4 million in early-stage funding from investors including DEPO Ventures and Startup Wise Guys. Investors may see value in its potential to capture market share across Central and Eastern Europe, where meal-kit penetration remains largely untapped.

q-gelatextechnologies.summary: Estonia-based Gelatex Technologies sells plant-based nanofibrous scaffolds to cultivated meat producers to provide structural integrity for growing cells. The startup has raised over €1.2 million in seed funding and conducted pilots with leading global cultured meat companies. Investors may care because its high-throughput manufacturing reportedly cuts scaffolding costs by up to 90 percent, tackling a critical scalability bottleneck in cellular agriculture.

05bace9e-b3f4-479b-8ad5-569c0bdfb641.summary: Tallinn-based Spindl develops an all-in-one restaurant management platform and cloud POS that unifies in-person ordering, kitchen workflows, self-service kiosks, and delivery channels for food service businesses. The company raised seed funding backed by Icebreaker.vc and serves multi-location restaurant chains across Estonia and Finland. Investors may value its ability to consolidate fragmented hospitality tech stacks while reducing operators' reliance on high-commission delivery aggregators.

q-fitlap.summary: Fitlap sells subscription-based personalized meal and workout plans to consumers, alongside co-branded healthy groceries through major Baltic supermarket chains. The bootstrapped business has attracted over 300,000 registered users and generates upwards of €600,000 in annual revenue. An investor might care because its profitable local operations and strong retail brand partnerships provide a proven foundation for international expansion.

61f7dce1-44bc-4ba9-aa37-86e81c368b64.summary: Membo operates an online grocery platform connecting consumers and offices directly with local farmers and European growers for fresh produce delivery. Backed by Y Combinator (S21), the Estonian startup raised seed funding in 2021. Investors showed interest because its shortened supply chain bypasses supermarket middlemen to deliver fresher goods with better economics for producers.

q-smartfood.summary: SmartFOOD sells calorie-controlled, ready-to-eat meal packages and snacks to health-conscious consumers across Estonia. Bootstrapped and unfunded since its 2017 launch, the company operates its own kitchen and delivery fleet, having prepared over one million meals. An investor might care because SmartFOOD has demonstrated steady customer retention and operational resilience as an established first mover in Baltic subscription nutrition.

ffb3f5ab-c33d-453e-b8e1-0dee62594378.summary: FitFood Estonia sells daily calorie-counted, ready-to-eat meal plan subscriptions to health-conscious consumers and busy professionals in Tallinn. The company has operated without disclosed venture funding, reporting over 1,000 customers served locally. Investors may appreciate recurring subscription cash flows tied to wellness trends, though logistical constraints in small geographic markets present a challenge for venture-scale growth.

q-fudy.summary: After shuttering delivery services, Estonia-based Fudy pivoted to in-restaurant ordering software and QR-code digital menus for hospitality venues. Backed by prominent Estonian entrepreneur Margus Linnamäe, the company generated €725,000 in 2022 revenue before restructuring to cut heavy delivery losses. Investors may watch whether its shift from capital-intensive delivery logistics to restaurant software can successfully achieve sustainable unit economics.

da399a05-c0f5-4f67-9a48-94c123797cb7.summary: Estonia-based Grab2Go sells AI-driven autonomous store hardware and management software to convenience retailers, grocers, and pharmacy chains. The company raised angel funding via EstBAN, launched pilots with partners like Selver, and listed on Nasdaq First North Baltic in 2023. An investor might care because its unmanned, 24/7 robotic stores directly mitigate rising labor shortages and high operating costs in retail.

q-superhands.summary: Tallinn-based Superhands sells IoT sensors and monitoring software to agriculture, forestry, and industrial enterprises to track soil, temperature, and environmental data. Supported by Estonian Business and Innovation Agency grants, it has deployed solutions with telecom operator Elisa and Estonia's State Forest Management Centre. Investors may value its proven enterprise traction and integrated hardware-SaaS model built for harsh, remote environments.

q-clickgrow.summary: Click & Grow sells automated indoor gardens and proprietary plant pods to consumers globally. Backed by Y Combinator, it raised an $11 million Series A with strategic backing from IKEA’s Ingka Group and Groupe SEB. Investors may value its razor-and-blade business model, which drives recurring revenue through repeat pod sales and subscriptions.

2e8e2468-2554-4502-bf39-1c8acc138236.summary: KappaZeta provides satellite-based crop monitoring and radar analytics to agricultural enterprises, insurers, and government agencies. The Estonian startup raised a 480,000 euro angel round alongside support from the European Space Agency. Investors may value its proprietary synthetic aperture radar processing, which delivers continuous, cloud-independent land monitoring across farming and forestry markets.

q-natufialabs.summary: Natufia Labs manufactures automated hydroponic indoor gardens that allow residential consumers and professional chefs to grow fresh herbs and greens year-round. The startup raised a $3.5 million Series A round led by the KAUST Innovation Fund. Investors may be drawn to its business model, which pairs high-ticket hardware with recurring seed-pod consumable sales across premium home and hospitality markets.

9438d126-c652-4192-b796-55b8c0cf3a5c.summary: Paul-Tech sells proprietary soil-sensing stations and data analytics software to farmers to monitor soil nutrients and moisture in real time. Backed by a €1.4 million seed round, the Estonian startup serves commercial agricultural clients across the Baltics, the Nordics, and the UK. Investors may care because its direct subsurface measurements optimize costly fertilizer use, solving critical data blind spots that optical satellite systems miss.

q-bugbox.summary: BugBox develops automated insect-rearing technology and supplies insect-derived protein and oils to food, animal feed, and pet nutrition manufacturers. Backed by approximately €1 million in funding and European grants, the company has established international research and distribution partnerships across Europe and Africa. Investors may care because its automated hardware addresses the high labor and production costs that historically hinder scalable insect farming.

q-boltfooddelivery.summary: Bolt Food sells on-demand restaurant meals and grocery delivery to consumers alongside marketplace and fulfillment services for merchants. The Tallinn-based platform has raised roughly $2 billion, including a €628 million Series F, and surpassed €2 billion in annual revenue across more than 200 million users. Investors care because cross-utilizing its existing ride-hailing fleet for deliveries provides substantial operational cost efficiencies over standalone food-delivery competitors.

272c479a-b826-47eb-b159-8d56d9999cb8.summary: VitalFields sold cloud-based farm management software to European farmers to track field operations and automate EU environmental compliance reporting. The company raised over $1.2 million from backers including Monsanto Growth Ventures and scaled to seven European countries before its 2016 acquisition by The Climate Corporation. Investors value it as proof that Baltic B2B software can solve cross-border regulatory pains and secure strategic corporate exits.

265404b2-bdc0-4363-8ba3-312919f84f22.summary: Woola manufactures protective packaging, including bubble wrap alternatives and padded envelopes made from discarded sheep wool, selling to e-commerce and luxury retailers such as LVMH. The company has raised over €5 million from investors including Metaplanet and Future Ventures. Investors may value its ability to convert an abundant, low-cost agricultural waste into commercial packaging as corporate ESG mandates and plastic bans accelerate.

4b621d7e-3f54-4d61-8a49-c8a0ec5a6f0e.summary: Starship Technologies provides autonomous sidewalk robot delivery services to grocery retailers and food delivery platforms like Uber Eats. Backed by over $250 million in funding, the company has completed more than 10 million commercial deliveries across eight countries. Investors care because its Level 4 autonomy cuts courier costs by three to four dollars per drop, solving last-mile unit economics at scale.

375a4dca-2d49-46a6-84f8-8d1041e16eb9.summary: Lingvist sells subscription-based, AI-driven adaptive language learning software directly to consumers and educational institutions. The company has raised over $15 million in funding from backers including Rakuten, Rubio Impact Ventures, and Skype co-founder Jaan Tallinn. Investors may find it attractive because its proprietary algorithms, originally developed by a CERN physicist, personalize vocabulary acquisition to accelerate fluency faster than traditional apps.

0db17623-fb96-4502-aafc-0582d115ef71.summary: Speakly sells a subscription-based language learning platform and corporate training to consumers and enterprise clients. The company raised a 900,000 euro seed round led by Superhero Capital and generates over 1 million euros in annual revenue. Investors may value its data-driven methodology that prioritizes statistically relevant vocabulary, offering an efficacy-first alternative to heavily gamified language apps.

q-clanbeat.summary: Clanbeat sells a digital personal growth and well-being platform to schools, helping students manage their mental wellness and self-directed learning. The company raised $1.2 million in seed funding led by Taizo Son’s Mistletoe, alongside Estonian angel investors from Pipedrive. Investors may care because increasing institutional mandates for student well-being provide strong B2B adoption opportunities across European and international school systems.

091758a8-6624-4ef0-bf8a-af2227e19a7f.summary: ALPA Kids sells localized, curriculum-aligned mobile learning games to parents and preschools for children aged 3–8. Supported by EU grants and early-stage backing, the platform has expanded into 14 languages across multiple European and international markets. Investors may appreciate its defensible niche in native-language early education, addressing regional language markets largely underserved by global edtech incumbents.

q-dreamapply.summary: DreamApply sells a SaaS admissions and student application management platform to higher education institutions. With around €2.7 million in annual revenue, it powers Estonia's national admission system and serves over 300 institutions across 40 countries. Investors may appreciate its high institutional retention and proven ability to expand internationally without reliance on heavy venture capital.

q-mentornaut.summary: Mentornaut operates a marketplace connecting primary and secondary school students with vetted private tutors for personalised online and in-person lessons. The startup has facilitated over 25,000 tutoring sessions and previously raised a €200,000 funding round led by the Estonian Business Angels Network. Investors may value its potential to capture rising regional demand for supplemental education using a lightweight, scalable marketplace model.

q-ekool.summary: eKool provides a digital school management and communication platform to schools, teachers, students, and parents, covering grading, attendance, and coursework. It dominates Estonia with adoption across roughly 90% of schools, reaching nearly 30% of the country's population, and has backing from investors including Trind VC. Investors may value its near-monopoly market position and high switching costs, which yield resilient recurring revenue and export potential.

ab69bd19-ea42-4df3-91d5-af13d6a0647b.summary: Bloomcoding sells live, interactive coding courses using AR and VR technologies to children aged 7 to 14. Headquartered in Estonia with operations across Central and Eastern Europe, the startup reached over 1,000 monthly students and raised a €1 million seed round backed by Credo Ventures and Inovo VC. Investors may value its capital-efficient expansion and immersive curriculum addressing underserved CEE markets.

600c5dab-594b-4398-a5b2-77253036fe8f.summary: Edumus sells a recruitment, training, and matching platform to schools, enabling working industry specialists to teach part-time elective courses. The startup raised €180,000 in pre-seed angel funding and has placed hundreds of professionals while piloting international expansion. Investors may care because it offers a scalable marketplace model addressing structural global teacher shortages by unlocking underutilized private-sector talent.

q-opiq.summary: Opiq provides a cloud-based digital textbook and learning environment to K–12 schools, pupils, and educational publishers. Developed by Star Cloud, the platform gained widespread adoption across Estonia through public sector contracts and has expanded internationally into Finland, Kazakhstan, and Kenya with no disclosed venture funding. Investors may appreciate its defensible publisher integration and proven ability to export national curriculum software into emerging markets.

q-flashka.summary: Flashka sells an AI-driven study platform that converts lecture notes and PDFs into flashcards, quizzes, and spaced-repetition workflows for students. The startup has raised a €1 million pre-seed round and reports over one million global users. Investors may find it compelling as a product-led challenger to legacy study tools, designed to deepen memory retention rather than simply provide AI shortcuts.

q-futuclass.summary: Futuclass sells curriculum-aligned virtual reality science modules and turnkey classroom kits directly to middle and high schools. Backed by grant and accelerator funding from Prototron and xEdu, the company has reached over 10% of Estonian schools. Investors may find it compelling because its validated learning outcomes and teacher co-design lower institutional procurement barriers as educational VR adoption expands.

q-foxcademy.summary: Foxcademy sells interactive digital science learning materials, tests, and analytics software to middle and high schools, teachers, and students. It achieved strong traction when Estonia's Ministry of Education funded licenses nationwide, leading to an eventual founder exit. Investors care because it demonstrated that early-stage edtech can achieve full national adoption and monetization through government contracts.

q-progracademy.summary: Progracademy provides online computer science, AI, and digital skills courses to K-12 students and schools using university-level tutors. The company raised approximately $309,000 in pre-seed funding backed by angel network G8i, though public filings reflect modest annual revenues. Investors may appreciate its dual-impact social enterprise model, which uses university mentors to scale accessible digital education across Spanish-speaking markets.

q-mapanda.summary: MaPanda provides an interactive video conferencing platform that enables educators and child psychologists to teach young children through real-time animated avatar characters. The startup has raised $1.3 million in funding to scale its gamified learning technology internationally. Investors may appreciate its differentiated approach to solving low attention spans and screen fatigue in early childhood remote education.

q-cognuseconurse.summary: Cognuse develops CoNurse, a mobile, hands-free guideline adherence and training platform sold to hospitals and healthcare providers to guide nursing staff through complex clinical procedures. The company has secured over $400,000 in early funding and innovation grants, with deployments across major Estonian hospital networks. Investors may value its ability to address acute nurse shortages by accelerating onboarding and reducing bedside clinical errors.

q-bizplay.summary: Bizplay sells gamified simulation kits, teacher training, and an online platform to schools and educators to teach entrepreneurship and financial literacy. While external funding is undisclosed, the company has established regional simulation hubs in Estonia and is targeting European expansion. Investors may care because its blended physical-digital model directly addresses increasing educational and governmental demand for youth financial literacy.

q-tutorid.summary: Tutor.id provides an AI-driven marketplace and SaaS management software—handling scheduling, lesson tools, and payments—to private tutors and students across hundreds of subjects. The company has secured early angel backing and grown to serve thousands of tutors across over 100 countries. Investors may appreciate its SaaS-enabled marketplace model, which incentivizes tutors to bring their own students, naturally reducing customer acquisition costs.

q-eliis.summary: ELIIS provides a SaaS management and communication platform for preschools, kindergartens, teachers, and municipal education authorities. It has achieved strong traction by securing over 80 percent of Estonian kindergartens, with more than 15,000 teachers using it daily across Europe. Investors may value its near-monopoly domestic market share and sticky public-sector relationships that provide a defensible base for international expansion.

q-loquiz.summary: Loquiz provides a software platform enabling educators, corporate trainers, and event organizers to build real-world interactive games, scavenger hunts, and tours. Operating largely bootstrapped without disclosed institutional funding, the service reaches over 220,000 annual players across more than 35 countries. Investors may value its cross-sector versatility, which diversifies SaaS revenue between budget-conscious schools and higher-margin corporate team-building clients.

q-triumfhealth.summary: Triumf Health develops a clinically backed mobile health game that provides mental wellbeing support to children, targeting healthcare providers, schools, and parents. The company has secured grant funding from Accelerate Estonia and EIT Health while partnering with academic institutions for clinical validation. Investors may appreciate its scalable, evidence-based approach to addressing widespread shortages in pediatric mental health resources.

q-speaktx.summary: SpeakTX provides a digital speech therapy platform with interactive exercises, treatment plans, and video consultations for therapists, schools, healthcare providers, and families. Adopted by over 6,000 users across roughly 500 Estonian institutions, the company is expanding internationally across Europe. Investors may care because it addresses severe global therapist shortages by scaling access and reducing clinician contact time by up to 30%.

q-kideocall.summary: KideoCall provides interactive, video-based language playgroups and camps to expat families seeking to maintain their children's native languages. Supported by Tehnopol's incubator and Estonian public grants, it has delivered over 1,000 session hours to hundreds of children globally. Investors may find interest in its monetization of underserved diaspora communities through coach-led active engagement rather than passive screen time.

q-duotale.summary: Duotale offers a screen-free bilingual audio storytelling platform designed for children, families, and childcare institutions to support early language acquisition. The startup has received European Union co-funding and built a library featuring more than 300 multilingual stories. Investors may value its screen-free positioning, which capitalizes on growing parental and institutional demand to reduce screen time while fostering early bilingualism.

q-praktikal.summary: Praktikal sells integrated science-teaching packages—combining hands-on experiment kits, curriculum materials, and a digital platform—to primary and secondary schools. Backed by Estonia's Good Deed Education Fund, it is used in over 300 schools and is expanding into Germany. Investors may value its strong domestic market penetration and ability to address widespread STEM teacher shortages through scalable, turn-key classroom solutions.

q-vocametrix.summary: Vocametrix sells a SaaS platform and APIs offering voice-controlled games and acoustic analysis tools to speech therapists, clinics, and healthtech developers. Affiliated with EdTech Estonia and Tehnopol, the company has no institutional funding publicly disclosed. Investors may care because it pairs gamified patient engagement with objective acoustic biomarkers, creating a scalable tool for both clinical and at-home speech therapy.

q-navicup.summary: Navicup provides an interactive map platform to schools and educators for creating gamified outdoor lessons, quizzes, and scavenger hunts. While institutional funding is undisclosed and revenues remain modest, the startup has showcased its software at international education events. Investors may care because it addresses demand for experiential, movement-based learning using standard smartphones without requiring schools to buy specialized hardware.

q-globalroom.summary: GlobalRoom sells an AI-powered education platform and administrative assistant to independent teachers, studios, students, and parents, offering lesson planning, automated booking, tutoring, and communication tools. Investors may care because it directly boosts client profitability within an opaque, multi-billion-dollar card network fee ecosystem.

71966585-9330-49a3-88ca-ea066445af45.summary: Kernolab provides embedded finance and banking-as-a-service APIs, allowing fintechs and non-financial companies to embed accounts, payments, and card issuing into their platforms. The company raised a $1 million pre-seed round led by Lighthouse Ventures and later acquired customer portfolios from core banking provider Paysolut. Investors may find it compelling because its middleware abstracts regulatory licensing, enabling rapid fintech monetization for enterprise clients.

78d8c462-91c9-4fc1-99a1-d2f865cff2b1.summary: Okredo provides an open-data and open-banking SaaS platform that sells credit scoring, partner risk assessment, and financial monitoring tools to European SMEs. The company has raised over €1.65 million in venture funding alongside a €1.2 million EU grant to expand its cross-border scoring capabilities. Investors may value its ability to monetize mandatory European open data through scalable, embedded B2B risk intelligence.

q-hesfintech.summary: HES FinTech sells modular, AI-powered lending and loan management software—covering origination, servicing, and collections—to banks, credit unions, and alternative lenders worldwide. The company is largely bootstrapped and has delivered over 160 lending automation projects across global markets. Investors may value its proven enterprise traction and capital efficiency in a large addressable market upgrading legacy banking infrastructure.

88202f2d-63e3-4497-a823-92561db90cec.summary: Spenfi provides an expense management platform with corporate payment cards, multi-currency accounts, and automated expense tracking to European small and medium-sized enterprises. The startup raised an €800,000 seed round led by Presto Ventures and operates in Lithuania and the Netherlands. Investors may value its regional foothold in consolidating fragmented SME financial workflows, though it faces entrenched competition from established European spend management players.

q-fininbox.summary: Fininbox provided a cloud-based core banking SaaS platform, including payment infrastructure and compliance tools, to credit unions, electronic money institutions, and fintechs. Operating without venture funding, it bootstrapped to roughly 1.4 million euros in annual revenue across more than 20 institutions before merging into Forbis in 2025. Investors should note its capital-efficient exit capitalizing on Lithuania’s regulatory fintech boom.

q-deepfin.summary: Vilnius-based DeepFin develops automated financial management, invoicing, and tax software tailored for freelancers and gig workers. The company raised €685,000 in pre-seed funding led by Superhero Capital and Iron Wolf Capital. Investors may care because Europe's expanding freelance economy creates a large, underserved market for dedicated solo-entrepreneur back-office infrastructure.

9a7ead3e-2ee0-4bce-b4d7-afe0a1ec8af1.summary: Oxipit sells AI diagnostic software to healthcare providers and radiology departments, notably ChestLink, which autonomously reports normal chest X-rays to reduce specialist workloads. The company raised around €5.4 million before being acquired by medical imaging leader Sectra in 2026. An investor would note its regulatory barrier to entry, having secured the first CE mark for fully autonomous radiological AI.

48eae846-56c6-45d8-be67-ad2696ca7920.summary: Ligence sells AI software to hospitals and cardiologists that automates cardiac ultrasound analysis and reporting, reducing manual examination times. The company has raised roughly €6.5M in funding from venture investors and European programs. Investors may find value in its FDA 510(k) clearance, which de-risks regulatory hurdles and unlocks direct commercial expansion into the United States.

q-fleming.summary: Fleming provides an AI-powered telemedicine app and digital health assistant that offers symptom checking, preliminary diagnoses, and remote consultations to patients and healthcare providers. The Vilnius-based startup has secured approximately 1.4 million dollars in seed funding from venture builder Kilo Health alongside European Union grants. Investors may value its access to Kilo Health's commercial distribution engine to scale automated triage across Europe.

q-revolab.summary: Revolab sells at-home blood testing kits and an AI-driven health tracking app directly to consumers and insured patients. The startup raised around €300,000 in seed funding, backed by Kilo Health, and achieved early revenue alongside local insurer reimbursement. Investors may care because its CE-certified medical device clearance and existing payer integration de-risk expansion into broader European preventive healthcare markets.

1e8af861-3dcb-4f84-913f-21e5ad49b53f.summary: Spike sells health data aggregation APIs and white-labeled, retrieval-augmented AI co-pilots to healthcare providers, digital health apps, and insurers. The startup has raised €3.2M in seed funding and serves clients including Seguros SURA and FITTR. Investors may value its moat of 300+ integrated wearable and clinical data sources, which lets enterprises deploy compliant health AI without building complex infrastructure.

q-tokitus.summary: Tokitus operates an online marketplace connecting European consumers and corporate employees with certified mental health therapists across multiple specialties and languages. The Vilnius-based startup raised a €125,000 pre-seed round from Venture Faculty to support expansion across Europe and the UK. Investors may value its multilingual matching, which targets a fragmented cross-border European market underserved by dominant English-centric telehealth platforms.

d5a2df93-a360-4575-9e78-940306b7dbc6.summary: Vilnius-based Openface sells AI-driven skin diagnostic assessments and custom-formulated skincare products directly to consumers. The startup has raised over $700,000 in early-stage funding from investors including Pitchdrive and Digital Disrupt. Investors may care because combining proprietary diagnostic algorithms with personalized cosmetic formulation drives higher customer stickiness in the high-margin direct-to-consumer beauty market.

7a8513a8-cb53-4253-9795-866302f7d3f2.summary: Pulsetto sells an app-controlled wearable vagus nerve stimulation device to consumers and defense personnel for stress, anxiety, and sleep management. The company reached over 300,000 users, grew revenue past $40 million in 2025, and raised a €2 million round from ScaleWolf. Investors may care about its proven consumer traction paired with expanding dual-use defense and enterprise applications.

44415bc4-cca7-41bd-be9e-2849aa1b057b.summary: Atrandi Biosciences develops microfluidic platforms and proprietary semi-permeable capsule technology, selling high-throughput single-cell analysis tools to life science researchers. The company has raised approximately €31M, including a Series A led by Lux Capital, and serves over 200 labs globally. Investors may value its patented technology, which enables complex, multi-step workflows that overcome traditional throughput bottlenecks in single-cell genomics.

q-biomatter.summary: Biomatter develops an AI platform that designs custom enzymes from scratch for biopharma, agriculture, and industrial biotech companies. It recently raised a €16.2 million Series A following €7 million in seed funding, delivering enzymes to enterprise clients like AstraZeneca and BASF. Investors care because Biomatter has proven commercial viability, with its engineered enzymes already deployed in market products while compressing development cycles from years to weeks.

q-walk15.summary: Walk15 sells a wellness and sustainable mobility platform to corporations and organizations, using step challenges to boost engagement and track ESG social impact. Backed by Coinvest Capital and angel syndicates, the company approached one million users and reached a €30 million valuation upon opening its Series A. Investors may value its ability to monetize corporate ESG mandates while expanding internationally into markets like Germany.

8ddc6c5b-0843-4362-9381-1b78258c68de.summary: Rauðás Games develops web and mobile card and puzzle games for global casual players, most notably operating the browser platform CardGames.io. The studio has scaled to millions of active users worldwide with no disclosed venture funding. Investors may value its low-overhead operational model combined with large, recurring organic traffic in evergreen gaming categories.
